This bonus-eligible role will support a very small team for financial planning, analysis, and reporting across corporate operations and multiple subsidiaries. This requires someone who can work independently and is self directed. The FP&A Analyst will play a key role in assisting with forecasting, budgeting, and performance analysis while providing data-driven insights for SaaS to support strategic and operational decision-making. This individual will partner closely with subsidiary finance teams and corporate stakeholders to ensure accurate financial reporting, thoughtful analysis, and consistent financial processes across the organization.

This is a hands-on role that requires strong attention to detail, intellectual curiosity, and a willingness to work deeply in the data. This role also provides the opportunity to contribute to the continued development of a formal FP&A function, including enhancing financial models, reporting frameworks, and analytical tools used by leadership to evaluate performance and support strategic decision-making.

* Support variance analysis and forecast updates across business units
* Assist with key assumptions like churn, ARR, MRR, Rev Rec 606 / GAAP and Net Rev (NRR)
* Support the annual budgeting process, including gathering inputs, validating assumptions, and tracking timelines.
* Forecasting and reforecasting based on monthly closes, highlighting risks.
* Maintain and enhance financial models for scenario planning, and decision support
* Partner with business unit finance teams to collect data and ensure consistency in reporting
* Support ad hoc financial analyses and modeling requests from leadership
* Assist in developing dashboards and reporting for key performance indicators such as revenue, bookings, and margins
* Prepare materials for quarterly business reviews and leadership presentations
* Identify opportunities to improve reporting, data quality, and FP&A processes
* Contribute to standardized reporting frameworks and best practices
* Support the use of automation and emerging analytics tools to enhance reporting and forecasting

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree
* Strong Excel experience, meticulous Excel spreadsheeting
* Minimum 3 years of financial analysis (FP&A) experience, preferably in SaaS or multi-business unit environments
* Experience in FP&A or corporate finance required (seeking Finance over Accounting)
* Strong financial modeling and analytical skills
* Experience with ERP and planning tools (e.g., Oracle, NetSuite, Adaptive) preferred
* Consulting or SaaS experience preferred.
* Basic understanding of SaaS metrics (ARR, bookings, churn, margins) preferred
* Strong communication and collaboration skills with the ability to work cross-functionally
* **HYBRID 3 days per week in the New York City corporate office**

description:
Link Logistics Real Estate (“Link”) is a leading operator of warehouses and business parks, specializing in last-mile logistics real estate. Established by Blackstone in 2019, the company connects consumption, technology, and the supply chain across its portfolio, which spans half a billion square feet. We put our people, customers, and communities first and find ways to make a conscious, positive impact where we live and work. Every day, we work to reinvent and lead our industry forward by thinking bigger and challenging the status quo.

We're hiring a hybrid **ML/Backend Engineer** to own the intelligence layer of Link's Analytics Engine. This is the connective tissue role: you'll design the pipelines that bring disparate real estate data to life, build the knowledge graphs and retrieval systems that make that data queryable by LLMs, and architect the backend services that surface insights to investment teams in real time.

You won't be handed a spec. You'll talk to investment analysts and asset managers, identify where analytical leverage is lost today, and build systems that close that gap — often combining classical ML, graph-based reasoning, and LLM-native workflows in the same solution.

**RESPONSIBILITIES:**

* Knowledge Graph & Retrieval — Design graph-based data structures encoding relationships across markets, assets, tenants, and transactions. Build retrieval pipelines (RAG, hybrid search, structured queries) that give LLMs accurate, contextually rich grounding.
* LLM Workflow Automation — Develop rule-based and agentic LLM workflows that automate investment analytical tasks. Own prompt engineering, eval frameworks, and production reliability.
* Data Pipelines — Build ETL/ELT workflows that ingest, normalize, and enrich large-scale internal and third-party datasets (property records, leasing data, macro signals, alt data). Every dataset should have a clear owner, update cadence, and quality SLA.
* Data Trust & Provenance — Build systems that make data trustworthy by design: lineage tracking from source to insight, confidence scoring on derived outputs, and clear attribution so analysts always know where a number came from and how fresh it is. Treat a bad comp or stale signal as a production incident.
* Backend API Layer — Develop and maintain APIs and services that expose ML outputs and structured data to front-end applications. Prioritize low-latency, reliability, and clean contracts with the application team.
* Collaboration — Work directly with investment and asset management teams to understand analytical needs and iterate quickly. Treat analyst trust as a first-class product requirement.

**QUALIFICATIONS:**

* 4+ years in ML engineering, backend engineering, or a role spanning both
* Hands-on experience shipping LLM-powered applications in production — RAG pipelines, prompt engineering, eval frameworks
* Strong Python skills; comfortable owning backend services and APIs end-to-end
* Experience with knowledge graphs or graph databases (Neo4j or similar)
* Proficiency building data pipelines at scale (Spark, Databricks, or equivalent)
* Deep sensitivity to data provenance — a track record of building systems that create analyst trust, not just claim it

Why finance matters here
  
  
Most finance roles inherit a business model. This one helps build one.
  
  
Our agents do work that accounting firms have always staffed with people. That makes the questions finance owns at Basis the questions that decide whether the company works: how you price hours of autonomous work, what margins look like when compute is a real cost of revenue, how far ahead of demand you build capacity, and where the next dollar of a fundraise should go. There is no playbook for this yet. You’ll help write it.
  
  
If you’ve spent years in banking, private equity, or venture modeling businesses like this from the outside, this is the chance to do it from the inside, with the data, the operators, and the ability to change the answer.
  
  
What you’ll do
  
  
This is not a reporting role. You’ll own the analysis end to end: framing the question, finding the truth in the numbers, deciding what it means, and then making sure the business acts on it. You’ll report to the Head of Finance and work across finance, revenue operations, go-to-market, product, and engineering.
  
  

* Own the models the company runs on. Revenue, headcount, unit economics, cash. Leadership makes decisions off your work, so it has to be right and it has to be legible.

* Chase down what doesn’t add up. When a metric moves and the explanation doesn’t sniff right, you go deep enough to find out why, whether that’s the data, the contract, or the Slack thread, and you come back with a real answer.
* Rebuild finance around AI. You’ll run experiments on where LLMs can take on finance work: the recurring reconciliation, the variance commentary, the board deck refresh. When you catch yourself doing a process by hand, you’ll ask whether you can build a skill, an agent, or a workflow that moves you from doing the work to reviewing it. Then you’ll build it.
* Be the finance team for the whole company. Field a founder’s question on runway and an engineer’s question on how commissions work with the same care. Deliver a brief to the leadership team on Monday; help a GTM lead read a capacity model on Tuesday.

**Location:**
NYC, Flatiron office. In-person team, five days a week.
  
  
Who you are
  
  

* An operator, not just an analyst. You’ve watched good analysis go nowhere and it bothers you. You measure your work by what changed, not by what got produced.
* Hyper curious. You ask why until you get an answer that holds up. You have a nose for when something is off and the patience to trace it to the source, and you use what you find to make better decisions.
* AI-forward. You already use AI to work faster and go deeper, and you want to know how far it can go. You’d rather run the experiment than read about it. You’re excited by the idea that the data entry gets done by an agent and your job becomes the judgment.

LoveShackFancy, founded in 2013 by Rebecca Hessel Cohen, is a global fashion, beauty, childrenswear, accessories, home, and lifestyle brand celebrated for its romantic, vintage-inspired aesthetic and cult-like community. In 2023, LoveShackFancy launched Beauty exclusively at Sephora, inviting millions into its rose-colored world of whimsy and celebration.
  
  
**About The Role**
LoveShackFancy is seeking a detail-oriented and analytical Financial Analyst to support financial planning, reporting, and business analysis across the organization. This role sits at the intersection of finance and operations, providing the CFO/COO with timely, accurate data and insights to guide strategic decision-making. The ideal candidate is comfortable working with large datasets, building financial models, and translating numbers into clear, actionable recommendations for leadership.
  
  
You will be working across the company’s operating divisions of retail stores, e-commerce, and wholesale on both the revenue and expense side.
  
  
Key Responsibilities
  
  
*Financial Planning & Analysis*

* Assist in the preparation of monthly, quarterly, and annual budgets and forecasts
* Support variance analysis (actuals vs. budget/forecast) and prepare commentary on key drivers
* Help build and maintain financial models for revenue, expenses, headcount, and cash flow
* Assist with ad hoc financial analysis to support strategic initiatives and business decisions

*Data Analysis & Reporting*

* Compile, clean, and analyze data from multiple sources (ERP, POS, e-commerce platforms, retail partners)
* Build and maintain dashboards and recurring reports (sales performance, channel profitability, KPIs)
* Identify trends, anomalies, and opportunities within sales, margin, and operational data
* Partner with cross-functional teams (merchandising, retail, e-commerce, operations) to gather and validate data

*Business Support*

* Support the CFO/COO with materials for leadership meetings, business decks, and reporting
* Assist with month-end close processes as they relate to reporting and reconciliations
* Track and analyze key business metrics across wholesale, DTC, and retail channels
* Help maintain and improve financial reporting templates, models, and processes for accuracy and efficiency

* Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business, or a related field
* 1–3 years of experience in FP&A, financial analysis, data analysis, or a related role (retail/apparel/consumer goods experience a plus)
* Advanced proficiency in Excel/Google Sheets (financial modeling, pivot tables, complex formulas)
* Experience with BI/reporting tools
* Familiarity with ERP and accounting systems
* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with high attention to detail
* Ability to synthesize complex data into clear, concise summaries for non-financial stakeholders
* Strong communication skills and comfort presenting to senior leadership
* Ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines in a fast-paced environment
* High degree of discretion when handling confidential financial information

title: Reporter, Founder Brew
description:
At Morning Brew Inc., we mix what you need to know with our unique brand of wit to attract, and build real relationships with, the next generation of business leaders. We speak to them like people, ensuring they get the context and insight needed to make decisions every day. Loyalty and trust are our most valuable currencies.

Whether scrolling, reading, watching, or listening, our audience trusts us for credible, entertaining business content that makes an impact on their personal and professional lives.

The Morning Brew team is clever, creative, and growing fast. Want in? Read on.

OVERVIEW

Founder Brew, a publication dedicated to exploring the real lives, decisions, and psychology of people building companies — from startups to small businesses to creative ventures—is looking for a reporter to cover the operational truths of being a founder.

Founder Brew explores what it’s like building a business—across startups, small businesses, and “unsexy” real-world companies—and is a publication focused on how current and aspiring founders can be better equipped to handle what comes their way.

Reporting is pragmatically optimistic, and divided between two modes: as-told-to, and traditional reporting. We publish the messy middle, resist PR gloss, and verify the facts behind first-person stories.

We’re looking for a reporter to ideate, research, and create journalism to help take this vertical to new heights.

**WHAT YOU'LL DO**

* Pitch, report, and write 3-5 stories per week for Founder Brew.

* Generate ideas for and lead/co-lead creation of non-newsletter editorial initiatives, enterprise pieces, and evergreen content, as we build out a digital home.

* Conduct research to support creation of key stories and inform longer-term projects.

* Create multimedia components that bring our stories to life in video and audio formats

* When needed, represent Founder Brew at live events, with the possibility of on-stage participation.

**WHAT YOU'LL BRING**

* Interest and expertise in business writing and reporting

* At least 3 years of journalism experience

* Ability to write in the Morning Brew style (engaging, informative, clever)

* Ability to quickly source up

* Understanding of how to analyze and draw conclusions from structured and unstructured data

* Understanding of how to leverage multiple platforms (email, social media, etc.) to engage with the target audience

* Self-starter attitude with ability to operate in a collaborative, quickly-changing environment

* Combination of attention to detail and creative, strategic thinking

* Excellent communication skills with a mindset for collaboration

* Ability to operate in a high-pressure environment with tight deadlines

**COMPENSATION** $40-45/hr. This is a temp-to-perm position.

**BRIEF BREW HISTORY**

Morning Brew Inc. was founded in 2015 by two entrepreneurial college students who noticed their peers were not consuming legacy media resources about business and finance news, but had a high desire to learn about those topics. What started as a small on-campus email has since evolved into a multi-channel media company that operates 20+ unique content franchises. All while maintaining our witty, honest and engaging tone that millions of loyal MBI audience members rely upon daily to better navigate the world.

In 2020 a majority stake in MBI was acquired by Axel Springer SE and in February 2025 that position was increased to full ownership of the business. Axel Springer SE is a family-owned, transatlantic media company headquartered in Berlin and New York that is committed to the values of a free and informed society. To learn more about Axel Springer SE and what defines us, visit http://axelspringer.com/en/what-defines-us.

Infinite Global is an international communications firm specializing in PR, Content & Campaigns, and Crisis & Litigation. Our clients are ambitious, complex organizations that need to engage with sophisticated audiences. We provide the experience, skills and insight to drive brands forward and, in special situations, to deploy strategies to defend clients from reputational risk.

We serve knowledge-intensive firms, with a focus on the legal and financial services sectors. Some of the world's largest, most profitable and most specialized law firms and financial services firms look to us for a nuanced understanding of their businesses, a clear sense of the kinds of stories that make news, and tested knowledge of when and how to engage the media.

Our unwavering client focus sets us apart and our approach and success earns accolades from our clients and peers. We are consistently named among PR News' "Agency Elite" and "Top Places to Work in PR" and have been recognized as the "Best PR Firm" by the National Law Journal seven times.

**What we're looking for**

A Staff Accountant to join Infinite's Finance & Operations team and take responsibility for the accuracy of the agency's books from one month to the next. You will own the recurring close work that keeps our financials reliable, including bank reconciliations, prepaid and accrual schedules, deferred revenue and payroll entries.

The role also creates room for the finance team to do more planning work, and you will be part of that: preparing the schedules and variance detail that forecasting and budgeting depend on, and helping analyze billable hours and utilization to connect staff time to client billing and project profitability.

**What you'd do**

**Month-end close**

* Perform monthly bank and credit card reconciliations for all US operating accounts, investigating and clearing reconciling items promptly.
* Maintain prepaid expense and accrual schedules, record monthly amortization and accrual entries, and reconcile each balance to its supporting detail.
* Track deferred revenue on client retainers and advance billings, recognizing revenue in line with GAAP and the terms of each engagement.

* Help analyze billable hours and utilization data from the agency's time tracking system, connecting staff time to client billing and project profitability.
* Prepare schedules and supporting documentation for the annual financial statement audit and respond to auditor requests in coordination with the team.

**Operations, controls and process**

* Support billing, accounts payable and accounts receivable, taking on day-to-day ownership of specific workstreams.

title: Senior Associate - Transaction Advisory Services
description:
**ABOUT VFG ADVISORY**

VFG Advisory LLC has spent over 20 years as a trusted advisor to privately held businesses, high-net-worth individuals, and nonprofit organizations. We go beyond tax and audit: we’re strategic partners who help clients grow, protect, and transition their wealth and business interests.

Our mission: deliver accounting and advisory services with integrity, insight, and innovation, built on long-term relationships and tailored solutions. We foster a collaborative, inclusive culture where professionals grow their careers while making a real impact for clients and community.

**POSITION OVERVIEW**

Transaction Advisory Services is part of our M&A team, which serves clients on both sides of a deal and runs the firm’s own acquisitions. For clients, we provide sell-side exit readiness and buy-side financial due diligence on transactions typically between $2M and $100M+, for a wide variety of businesses, including manufacturing, distribution, professional services, technology, retail, construction, and more. For the firm, we run VFG’s own acquisitions of CPA firms, from first look through close and integration. The M&A team also takes on financial due diligence outside of M&A, such as forensic accounting, divorce cases, and sales tax audits, as well as Office of the CFO work such as securing financing, carve-outs, and customized KPIs. The team is small and growing, backed by a loyal client base and an active referral network. It works closely with firm leadership and includes colleagues with Big 4 and public accounting backgrounds.

Most transaction advisory roles put you on one side of one kind of deal. Here you will see how a deal looks from the seller’s side, the buyer’s side, and the principal’s chair. On client engagements, you will work directly with owners buying or selling a business, for whom the deal is often the largest transaction of their lives, and help them get it right. On VFG’s own acquisitions, we are the buyer and the decisions are ours, and you will work alongside the firm leadership making them.

Transaction Advisory Services is the core of the role. Around it, the mix moves with deal flow and client demand: some months bring one of our own acquisitions, others a forensic project or a loan package. This role suits someone who wants that variety and enjoys project work.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Transaction Advisory Services (~60%)**

* Perform buy-side Quality of Earnings (QoE) engagements, from initial request list and management discussions through databook, report, and final presentation.
* Own the core analyses of each QoE engagement, including Adjusted EBITDA, revenue quality and customer concentration, P&L and margins, net working capital, and cash proofs.
* Lead sell-side transaction advisory engagements: prepare companies for sale, build Adjusted EBITDA workpapers, and guide owners, often selling for the first time, through the due diligence process.
* Normalize cash- and tax-basis books, work through inconsistent accrual accounting and unusual journal entries, and turn messy data into analysis that stands up.
* Present findings, defend positions, and explain accounting concepts in plain terms to clients, counterparties, bankers and brokers, and their advisors.
* Manage multiple engagements at once and keep each one moving against its timeline.

**VFG Acquisitions (~20%)**

* Run diligence on active acquisitions, including normalized financials, cash proofs, revenue analysis, working capital pegs, staffing and capacity, and key risks.
* Build pro forma models and projections, and draft board memos and presentations on deal terms, rationale, and findings.

A career at Optimum means you'll be enabling progress and enhancing lives by providing reliable, high-speed connectivity solutions that keep the world connected. If you are resourceful, collaborative, and passionate about delivering consistent excellence, Optimum is for you!
  
  
**Job Summary**
The Sr. Analyst, FP&A will focus on high impact projects and initiatives within the Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A) function - including the preparation and development of operating budgets, forecasts, short and long-term business plans (LRP), variance, and trend analysis. This role will assist with consolidation and distribution of daily, weekly, and monthly statistical and financial reports and analysis. The ideal candidate will have previous experience with the preparation and analysis of budgets and forecasts, as well as aspirations to further develop a career in Finance.

* Direct responsibility for preparing the annual budget and monthly forecasts for assigned business areas.
* Work closely with business leaders to develop budget/forecast/LRP that reflects operational and financial goals of the company and act as a resource to help achieve these goals.
* Assist in the consolidation and reporting of the budgets and forecasts for the department.
* Consolidation and reporting for all operating expenditures.
* Assist in the monthly review, analysis and reporting of consolidated operating expenditures.
* Assist in the preparation and consolidation of variance analysis.
* Conduct financial and statistical analysis, reporting and tracking for all assigned business areas, supported by commentary and analysis.
* Develop, report, and maintain routine and ad-hoc financial analysis.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor's Degree in Finance, Accounting, or related field.
* Ability to analyze large amounts of data and develop models for ad-hoc analysis.
* 4+ years' experience in Accounting or Finance, including previous experience in preparation and analysis of budgets and forecasts.
* Prior experience with financial reporting tools (Hyperion, Oracle, Essbase).
* Excellent oral and written communications skills, with the ability to interact with employees and leaders at all levels.
* Detail oriented with the ability to analyze problems, probe facts, question assumptions, and provide solutions and alternatives.
* Strong Excel skills including advanced formulas, pivot tables, graphs and charts.
* High degree of integrity, strong communication skills.
* Ability to analyze and solve problems using fact-based decision-making.

At Optimum, every action and interaction we take part in, is driven by our three Guiding Principles: Do What’s Right, Drive One Optimum, and Make It Happen. title: Senior FP&A Associate
description:
Madhive is the leading independent and fully customizable operating system built to help local media professionals build profitable, differentiated, and efficient businesses. Madhive empowers sales teams to extend their reach into streaming and connects local advertisers with the communities they serve. Madhive’s platform provides the unique ability to reach local audiences at national scale, with premium supply partnerships and end-to-end tools for planning, targeting, and measuring full-funnel campaign outcomes. Powering campaigns for over 30,000 small and medium businesses per day, Madhive is driving the evolution of local media.
  
  
Madhive is looking for a
**Senior FP&A Associate**
to join our Strategic Finance team in New York. The successful candidate will own core forecasting, reporting, and business partnering infrastructure, directly informing pricing, investments, and stakeholder reporting.
  
  
This is a builder's role. You will design and automate maturing financial processes, establish operational standards, and communicate complex insights clearly across the business.
  
  
You will report to the Director, Strategic Finance and partner closely with all the departmental leaders across the business.
  
  
This role is based out of our New York City headquarters at 225 Broadway. We operate on a hybrid model, and the ideal candidate will work from the NYC office 3 days per week as needed for team collaboration, close cycles, and planning sessions.
  
  
**What You'll Do**
**Planning & Forecasting**

* Own the integrated operating model — maintain a multi-schedule three-statement model with scenario testing, clear source mappings, and documented logic changes.
* Build the annual budget & planning cycle across revenue, OpEx, headcount, and cash alongside department heads.
* Manage headcount and compensation planning, keeping forecasts reconciled with HRIS census and approved compensation structures.
* Model revenue dynamics including platform fees vs. media pass-through, take rates, gross vs. net revenue, and AdTech unit economics.
* Design the planning rhythm — establish budget-vs-actuals reviews, spend approval workflows, and monthly business reviews.

**Reporting & Close**

* Support the monthly close alongside Accounting by preparing accruals, reviewing actuals, and analyzing variances.
* Deliver monthly reporting packages with variance analysis against budget, forecast, and prior periods.
* Maintain system reconciliations, including NetSuite-to-Looker bridges with fully documented variance drivers.
* Analyze profitability across products, business lines, customers, and channels.
* Track core KPIs including ARR, NRR, gross/logo retention, cohort profitability, CAC payback, and gross margins.
* Prepare stakeholder materials for Board, lender, and investor presentations, including debt covenant calculations.

**Controls & Data Integrity**

* Ensure data accuracy by tying out deliverables against approved models and control totals before distribution.
* Validate source data from NetSuite, Looker, Salesforce, and HR systems before model ingestion.
* Maintain version control and document all formula, logic, and mapping updates across shared tools.

**Business Partnering**

* Partner with department leaders across the organization to evaluate spend and stress-test assumptions.
* Manage tech & AI economics — forecast cloud spend, build cost attribution tags, and track AI/LLM unit economics.

**Systems, Automation & Data**

* Streamline FP&A workflows by optimizing ERP and planning systems to reduce manual processes.
* Standardize metrics & reporting in collaboration with BI, Systems, and Accounting.
* Document financial processes to ensure scalability, audit readiness, and continuity.

**Who You Are**

* 4–6 years of experience in FP&A, strategic finance, corporate finance, investment banking, or consulting.
* Bachelor's degree in Finance, Economics, Accounting, or a quantitative field.
* Advanced financial modeling experience building integrated 3-statement models from scratch.
* Strong control discipline with a proven track record of error-free, board-grade deliverables.
 [...] * Experience with Board and lender reporting or debt covenant tracking.
* Big 4, investment banking, or consulting training.
* Hands-on experience with ERPs/planning tools (NetSuite, Adaptive, Pigment, Anaplan).
**You'd Be a Great Fit If**
* Detail-oriented with high accuracy standards and a strong self-check discipline.
* Cross-functional influencer who can partner across teams to drive financial discipline.
* Tech & AI-forward mindset to leverage modern tools for speed and deeper analysis.
* Resourceful problem solver comfortable navigating ambiguity and shifting priorities.
**What Success Looks Like**
**In your first 90 days**
* Master the business model, own core reporting deliverables, and establish model audit controls.
**By the end of your first 6 months**
* Deliver reliable operating models, timely close reporting, and automated FP&A workflows.
The approximate compensation range for this position is $130,000-$160,000. The actual offer, reflecting the total compensation package and benefits, will be determined by a number of factors, including the applicant's experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity among our team.
**We are Madhive**
Madhive is a dynamic, diverse, innovative, and friendly place to work. We embrace our differences and believe they fuel our creativity. We come from varied backgrounds and think that’s important. Whether it’s taking ideas from previous lives and applying them in different ways or creating something completely new, we are all trail-blazing team players who think big and want to make an impact.

That is why we are committed to creating a work environment that actively values, appreciates, and respects everyone. We encourage applications from people with a wide variety of backgrounds and experiences.
  
  
Consider a career at WMG and get the best of both worlds – an innovative global music company that retains the creative spirit of a nimble independent.
  
  
**A Little Bit About Our Team**
**The Corporate Finance Department at WMG oversees the Company’s financial operations in partnership with WMG’s labels, business units and corporate functions. The team is responsible for financial planning and analysis, budgeting and forecasting, management reporting, accounting oversight and financial compliance across the Company.**
****Your Role****
**Reporting to the Senior Manager, Corporate Finance, the Senior Analyst will play a hands-on role in the management of centrally managed Corporate functions and Recorded Music functional areas.**
**You will take ownership of key day-to-day budgeting, forecasting, reporting and accounting activities for Corporate functions. Acting as a key finance partner, you will help department leaders understand their financial performance, lead their budgets and make informed business decisions.**
**This is a hands-on role offering broad exposure to the financial operation of a global music company, regular interaction with finance and non-finance stakeholders, and the opportunity to develop within a collaborative, high-performing team.**
****Here You'll Get To:.****

* Work closely with the Shared Service Center and other Finance teams to ensure costs are accurately recorded in the general ledger and align with Company policies.
* Prepare comprehensive month-end reporting packages and monthly forecast materials, including analysis of material spend and variances against budget, forecast and prior year.
* Partner with Corporate function leaders and budget owners to understand financial performance, identify risks and opportunities, and maintain accurate forecasts.
* Support the annual budget, monthly forecasting and long-range planning processes, including the development and maintenance of supporting financial models.
* Compile and analyze Corporate spend information used in senior-management, Board and external reporting materials.
* Provide financial oversight of operational activities, including invoice coding and submissions, vendor setup, purchase order tracking, commitments and project cash-outflows.
* Maintain strong follow-up on outstanding items, results and forecast assumptions across multiple collaborators.
* Continuously find opportunities to automate processes, improve financial controls and streamline recurring reporting.

Spring Health is a global mental health company on a mission to eliminate every barrier to mental health. We're building a world where getting support is simple, personal, and built around the person, so care can continue through every job, move, health plan, and life stage.

 - Care Operations managers report that workforce changes are accurate and well documented.

 - Frontline teams report that workforce support is responsive, accurate, and clearly communicated.

 - High attention to detail and strong organizational skills for managing complex schedules and frequent coverage changes.

 Palmetto is a consumer energy platform that provides homeowners with a single destination to discover, purchase, finance, install, monitor and manage home energy products and services. By offering one integrated platform across solar, battery storage, HVAC, heat pumps and more, Palmetto helps homeowners make home energy more affordable, reliable and accessible. Today Palmetto serves hundreds of thousands of homeowners, across 30+ states, building the operating infrastructure for the consumer energy transition, one home at a time.
 Our employees are our most valuable resource. We foster a promote-from-within culture that prioritizes talent development, career growth, and purpose-driven work. Palmetto offers a comprehensive benefits package—including unlimited PTO, medical, dental, and vision coverage, paid parental leave, retirement plans, and more—so you can have it all both personally and professionally. Palmetto prioritizes people, planet, and profit—backed by a culture that values collaboration, impact, and balance. Join us in building a brighter, cleaner world.
 Location 
 This position will be based in New York, NY.
 Reporting 
 This role will report to the Manager, Capital Markets.  
 Summary of Role  
 The Capital Markets Analyst will support capital markets activities spanning reporting, data operations, and business analysis to advance Palmetto Finance's funding strategies. This person will be a critical connector between the capital markets function and internal business teams, bringing a strong understanding of the business alongside sharp analytical and technical skills. This is an individual contributor role.
 Strategic & Tactical 
- Own monthly and quarterly reporting across Palmetto's capital markets funding structures, including tax equity funds, ABS issuances, and warehouse facilities
- Download, manage, and analyze large datasets to support fund reporting and investor requirements
- Build and maintain reporting templates for new and existing funding structures, partnering with technology teams to drive automation over time
- Develop a deep understanding of Palmetto's business, including how solar loan origination, customer relationships, and financing products connect to capital markets activity
- Support FP&A, treasury, and cash forecasting activities as they relate to Palmetto Finance
- Liaise with Corporate Finance, Treasury, Asset Management, and Accounting to ensure transparency and alignment on all things Palmetto Finance
- Identify opportunities to improve reporting workflows, data processes, and cross-functional efficiency
- Build and maintain strong working relationships with internal teams including Data Analytics, Operations, and Technology
 Qualifications 
- Bachelor's degree in Finance, Economics, Business, or related field
- 1–3+ years of experience in a finance, analytics, or business operations role; residential solar, FP&A, treasury, investor relations, or utility experience strongly preferred
- Strong business acumen;  you understand how a business works and can connect financial data to operational reality
- Solid analytical and Excel skills; experience with Microsoft Fabric or similar data platforms is a strong plus
- Comfortable working with large datasets and building structured, repeatable reporting outputs
- Proactively takes ownership of tasks, follows through independently, and coordinates across teams to get things done
- Highly motivated and able to thrive in a fast-paced, customer-centric environment where priorities shift quickly
- Strong interpersonal and communication skills; can work across finance, technology, and operations teams effectively
 Employment is contingent upon the successful completion of a background check.  
 Equal Employment Opportunity

description:
About Evidence Action 
 At Evidence Action, we deliver data-driven interventions that transform lives at an unprecedented scale. We identify neglected global health issues and deploy proven solutions, forging healthier futures for generations.
 Our model operationalizes leading academic research (including from Nobel-winning economists). We measure progress and outcomes at every stage to ensure we’re making a real impact for people living in poverty and suffering from preventable or treatable health issues. Operating across 11 countries, our team of 900+ has reached over 500 million people, working closely with governments to scale these interventions.
- Our Deworm the World program has delivered over 2 billion treatments, significantly reducing worm prevalence and generating more than $23 billion in lifetime productivity gains. 
- Through Safe Water Now, we’ve saved the lives of over 15,000 children. 
- Our Accelerator explores untapped opportunities in global health, testing low-cost interventions with the greatest potential to save and improve lives. 
 At Evidence Action, your colleagues are your greatest asset. You'll partner with high-caliber colleagues in an environment blending innovation, autonomy, and teamwork. Our team excels in disruptive thinking and believes in rolling up our sleeves to get things done. If you're looking to work flexibly and with purpose, join a team that delivers measurable change for millions.
 About the Finance & Operations Team 
 Our Global Strategic Finance and Budgeting team is committed to empowering programs to achieve their impactful goals by delivering insightful financial information, analysis, and reporting, aiding financial planning and budgeting. This includes evaluating new opportunities through the financial lens, maintaining long-term financial plans, and contributing to ad-hoc special projects that align with our financial strategy and support Evidence Action’s growth. 
 Reporting to our Manager of Program Finance, you will be a hands-on financial partner to Safe Water in India, Deworm the World, Iron and Folic Acid programs ensuring teams have timely data to make decisions. You will be working closely with program leadership and colleagues across regional and country finance, cross cutting teams supporting on budgeting and forecasting, donor financial reporting, Planful and data management, and implementing-partner finance across the portfolio.
 Key Responsibilities 
 1. Planful and Financial Systems (35%)
- Support the migration of program budgets from Excel into Planful by analyzing discrepancies across systems, validating budget assumptions and allocations, and working with relevant teams to resolve issues and ensure financial accuracy
- Apply consistent budget structures, activity coding, and reporting categories linked to the chart of accounts.
- Build and maintain financial reports, templates, and guidance that improve access to financial information and enable program teams to effectively use financial data for planning and decision-making.
- Maintain program budgets, forecasts, and actuals in Planful, monitor the integrity of financial data, and build expertise as a go-to Planful resource for India program teams. 
 2. Budgets and Forecasts (30%)
- Partner with the Finance & Operations lead to serve as the point of contact for program teams during the budget process.
- Monitor budget versus actuals, incoming funds, commitments, and grant balances; analyze variances, identify underlying drivers and emerging financial risks, and flag areas requiring attention.
- Support the maintenance and update of multi-year financial models and scenarios assessing the financial implications of changes in program plans, staffing, and operational assumptions.
- Prepare clear financial summaries and analyses for program leadership and Program Finance reviews to support informed resource allocation and financial decision-making.
 3. Donor Reporting and Grants (25%)
- Prepare donor financial reports and supporting schedules with Accounting and Grants and Compliance, ensuring accuracy and consistency with donor requirements.
- Monitor restricted grants, including spending against budget, allowable costs, reporting deadlines, and closeout requirements; proactively flag potential compliance or budget risks.
 [...]  Requirements 
- You have 3-5 years of experience and hold a Bachelors degree in a relevant field (e.g. International Development, Economics, Finance, Math, Statistics) or a Master’s degree and 2+ years of experience. 
- You have demonstrated financial analytics and budgeting experience with the ability to translate financial and technical data into clear, informative analysis that supports decision-making.
- You are comfortable using Excel: you are proficient with core functions and formulas, and can manage complex spreadsheets and models as assumptions change.
- You are a process-oriented thinker who identifies areas for improvement, suggests how to make systems run more smoothly, and acts on those opportunities within your workstreams.
- You absorb new information quickly and are comfortable building processes and finding answers to questions, including supporting the scoping of new work and new geographies.
- You work collaboratively, seeking to elicit and understand needs, opportunities, and key messages.
- You manage your own workload, reprioritizing as program needs evolve and escalate when you are at capacity, and communicate about priorities and progress to relevant stakeholders.
- You are curious about technology, including AI, try new tools responsibly, and share what you learn with the team.

- Manage the network: Keep track of key relationships and follow-ups across business partners, enterprise functions, and external stakeholders.
 What this role is not 
- Not a people-management role. You’ll lead through influence, driving outcomes across teams that don’t report to you.
- Not a line-of-business operator seat. You won’t run a P&L or a production team day to day. Instead, you’ll get a rare, enterprise-level view of how a multi-vertical transaction services business is built and scaled.

title: Strategic Finance
description:
THE GAP NO ONE HAS FILLED

Every complex system in America has a profession whose job it is to be your trusted guide. You have a lawyer for legal. An accountant for taxes. A financial advisor for your money. Healthcare, a trillion-dollar industry that's arguably the most complex and touches every single family, leaves us on our own.

99% of care happens when someone steps outside the four walls of a doctor's office. Hera is creating a new profession in healthcare to fill that gap: the Hero, a dedicated senior care expert for your family. Our Heroes educate, coordinate, and advocate for the most vulnerable population in the healthcare system. We’re covered by insurance, so we can serve every family in America.




BUILDING THE MOST TRUSTED INTERFACE OF HEALTHCARE

We are in the business of trust.

We're designing for the most emotionally charged moments of our customers' lives; the bar isn't just delight, it's trust. Hera's brand promise is simple: care worthy of our parents. This promise is our moat.

It's what physicians refer to, families buy, what Heroes deliver, and what the product must unlock and enforce at every touchpoint.




OUR PRODUCT CHALLENGE 

The bottleneck isn't demand, it's supply. There aren't enough experts to serve every family who needs us. To scale to all of America, we have to unbundle expertise from the human so that anyone who can foster human connection can become a Hero. 

The problem is that this expertise is tribal knowledge. One social worker knows how to expedite Medicaid in New York, another knows which home-visiting PT families actually love. It's trapped in people's heads.  

To solve this,  our platform captures every interaction and turns it into compounding intelligence that makes every user smarter. Think Waymo: expert humans do the driving today, and every mile they log trains the system so that tomorrow, anyone — even with zero healthcare background — can perform like a 20-year veteran. The hard part is building a system that knows what to trust, what's gone stale, what's local versus universal, and how to surface the right insight at the right moment. Get it right and you've scaled healthcare expertise beyond the lucky few who know the right person.

We wrote more on why and how we are building this technology here. https://hellohera.notion.site/what-endures-when-execution-is-free




OUR FOUNDING TEAM

We've raised $34M from Accel and Bain Capital Ventures and 10x'd revenue over the last 6 months organically through close partnerships with Weill Cornell, NYU Langone, UCSF, USC, and Mount Sinai. Chief of Geriatrics at Weill Cornell and Director of Geriatrics at NYU Langone have joined us as clinical advisors. CFO of Mount Sinai has invested in us. 
The customer feedback is the most positive our team has seen in our careers. Along the way, we threw an art show for an 88 year old artist that went viral https://ny1.com/nyc/all-boroughs/news/2026/02/19/88-year-old-brooklyn-painter-sells-art-for-the-first-time and a talent show https://www.instagram.com/reel/DZi3YmESZ6Q/?igsh=MTR3cjg4ZmJvb2NyZQ%3D%3D where every act is over 65.
You’ll build Hera alongside co-founders Jenny https://www.linkedin.com/in/jennydlee/, Myles https://www.linkedin.com/in/mylesnovick/ & Connie https://www.linkedin.com/in/jingyi-connie-kang/ and a team from Palantir and Headway. We are in person in NYC. Read our story and watch our launch video here https://hellohera.com/about.







JOIN US TO BUILD OUR STRATEGIC FINANCE FUNCTION

At most companies, finance is a reporting function: close the books, build the budget, explain the variance. This role is different; it is not an FP&A role. At Hera, you're in the room for every big investment we make, and you own the math behind it. Every Hero we hire, every market we open, every payer we contract with and every program we bill under is a bet with a cost and a return that either compounds or doesn’t. You’ll turn those bets into numbers we trust, then go out and move the numbers. 
You’ll bring the analytical rigor of a seasoned financier and the ethos of a strong operator: surgical execution, relentless truth seeking and an obsession with greatness. You'll work through hard tradeoffs in the business and then go make it happen.
PROBLEMS YOU’LL OWN
 - Unit economics. Both sides of it. On the Hero side: what it costs to recruit, train, ramp and retain a Hero, how many families a Hero can serve before the 20% starts falling behind, and where our platform bends that curve. On the family side: what it costs to find and onboard a family, how much value we deliver to families, and how long they stay with us. You’ll build the model that ties the two together, then work with growth teams to move its inputs.

 - The company operating model. Own the equation that connects growth inputs (patient referrals, Hero capacity, product levers) to revenue and margin. Set targets with each team and run the cadence that holds us to them.
 - Capital strategy. Cash planning, board and investor materials, fundraising prep. Treat capital as a scarce resource, and point it at the highest-leverage bets.
You’ll own the plan and the model, but you won’t spend your week reconciling accounts or writing variance commentary. If you love figuring out why a number is what it is and then fixing it, we'd love to chat.

ABOUT THE OPPORTUNITY

The goal of this project is to train AI to think like real financial professionals: how models are built from scratch, how assumptions are structured, and how credit and debt decisions are made using financial models.

 

This is a hands-on Excel modeling role where you will build detailed credit and debt models from a blank spreadsheet and explain your logic. We evaluate two distinct technical tracks under this posting:

 - Credit: 3-statement borrower models, cash flow-based lending, debt sizing, covenant modeling, loan structuring, and downside cases. (If your experience is in leveraged finance, direct lending, or project finance, your background fits our Credit area).

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Model and link 3-statement borrower financials, amortization schedules, payment-in-kind (PIK) interest, dynamic cash sweeps, DSCR, and debt covenants (Credit track).
   
    

 - Structure bond pricing, yield curves, and fixed income portfolio construction models from the ground up (Debt track).
   
    

 - Review, debug, and improve model accuracy by identifying incorrect assumptions, broken logic, and structural risks.
   
    

 - Clearly explain financial logic, decision-making, and why a model works in structured English.
   
    


MUST-HAVE REQUIREMENTS

Candidates from Investment Banking or Corporate Finance are considered only with top-tier backgrounds.

 - Proven ability to build full financial models from a blank spreadsheet in Excel without using pre-built templates, plug-ins, or AI tools.

   - Credit Track: Hands-on experience structuring 3-statement borrower models, debt sizing, DSCR and covenants, amortization schedules, PIK interest, cash sweeps, and downside cases.

THIS ROLE IS / THIS ROLE IS NOT

Most fund finance seats are a person doing the work. This one is a person deciding what the work should be, then building the agents that do it.

Equi runs alternative strategies through several layers of onshore and offshore vehicles. That structure is what lets us bring hard-to-access strategies to advisors and family offices, and it makes the accounting, money movement and reporting more demanding than a ten-person firm suggests. We need one senior leader to own all of it, and to make it run on systems rather than on anyone's attention.

About Equi

Equi gives investors the tools to own their financial future. We bring institutional-quality alternative strategies, in hedge funds and private credit, that are hard to get access to, to wealth advisors, family offices and institutions. We build and manage multi-strategy funds and white-labeled funds for some of the best independent multi-family offices and advisory firms in the country, pairing Silicon Valley tech with Wall St expertise.

Our growth is accelerating rapidly. We just launched the largest client in our history, have several more signed or close, and are targeting a multiple of today's assets. We're about ten people, so every hire here shapes a function rather than inheriting one. We hire builders and team players that aren't afraid of taking a high degree of ownership.

The role

You'll own finance and fund operations for the fund complex and the management company, reporting to the CEO. That means the NAV cycle and the reconciliation behind it; capital calls, distributions, redemptions and onboarding; every wire and the controls around it; budget, treasury, audit and tax; investor reporting; and the setup of every new vehicle.

We own our books. You'll build and run an internal shadow NAV for every vehicle, one we're 100% confident in, and reconcile it against our administrator every cycle. When the numbers disagree, you decide the firm's position, and you hold our administrator, auditor, counsel and banks to a standard. Partners should be checking our work, not telling us what our numbers are.

When something recurring is manual, you build the thing that removes it instead of absorbing it or hiring for it. These agents touch investor money, so the bar is production, not demo: each one is checked against an independent source, has evals that catch a regression when a prompt or model changes, and hands off to a person instead of failing silently. If you can't say how you'd know an agent got something wrong, it doesn't go live.

What success looks like in year one

 - We run our own shadow NAV on every vehicle and trust it fully, every close reconciles it against the administrator, and nothing reaches an investor without your sign-off

 - Agents handle statement intake, reconciliation, exception flagging and the first pass of reporting, each with checks that prove it right

 - Every wire runs on documented controls with dual approval, and an auditor could walk through them today

 - Audit, tax and regulatory deadlines are met, and new vehicles launch without the existing complex slipping

 - Investors and advisers get accurate reporting on time, and the firm's financial picture is current instead of rebuilt at month-end

What you'll own

 - Our own books: an internal shadow NAV on every vehicle, reconciled against the administrator each cycle, with your final sign-off

 - Fund operations: capital calls, distributions, redemptions, subscriptions and investor onboarding

 - Money movement: cash across operating and fund accounts, and approval authority on every wire

 - Corporate finance: fund expense budget and allocation, burn and runway, board reporting, payroll and benefits

 - Audit, tax and compliance: counterpart to the auditor and tax preparer, working with our compliance partner

 - Launches: the financial setup of each new vehicle, with outside counsel on structure and documents

 - Investor service: reporting that goes out on time, and fast, honest answers to investors and advisers
 - The provider network: administrator, auditor, tax preparer, counsel, prime brokers and banks, held to a written standard
Who you are
 - Deep fund accounting and operations: 8 to 12 years running or overseeing the finance and operations of a multi-vehicle fund complex, at an administrator, hedge fund, multi-strategy or private-markets manager, or outsourced fund-CFO practice. You've built or run a shadow NAV, and you find the error in a draft NAV before anyone else does.
 - A builder: you've shipped agents and automations, not just used AI. You can tell us what you built in the last six months, what it changed, where it broke, and how you proved it right before trusting it with real numbers.
 - Technical range beyond spreadsheets: coding agents, scripts, no-code automation, small internal apps. You don't need to be an engineer, but you pick up a new tool over a weekend.

 - Fund legal fluency: you've worked closely with fund counsel and know what a PPM, side letter or subscription agreement commits the firm to.
 - Hands-on: you've worked somewhere small enough that you did the work yourself. If the close always belonged to a team two levels down, this isn't the seat.
 - Direct: you close loops, and you tell the CEO plainly when a number is wrong.
Nice to have: layered multi-vehicle structures, offshore vehicles and their audit cycle, ERISA and plan-asset monitoring, or a CPA or legal background (or equivalent depth earned another way).
How we work
Team-first, flat and direct. Ideas win on merit, people argue a position and change their mind when the evidence says so, and nobody stays narrowly in lane when there's an adjacent fire. To learn more, visit www.industriousoffice.com/careers http://www.industriousoffice.com/careers.



About the Role

Industrious signs new landlord partnerships every year, and the number is growing as our business development team expands. Before any of those deals move forward, someone has to check that it holds together: that the assumptions are sound, that the start date, budgets, rent, pricing, and returns all track, and that the figures from design and construction have carried through correctly. As a Real Estate Associate on our Real Estate Transactions team that will be your job!



You will underwrite assigned deals in Excel, explain what drives their returns, and flag where a deal is tight, whether on pricing, occupancy, or CapEx. Our business development colleagues make the call on whether a deal goes ahead, and your analysis is what they rely on to make it well. You will work with Design, Construction, Finance, and other teams to make sure every number is right, supporting several business development colleagues as deal flow shifts.



Our approach to underwriting is different from a traditional real estate shop, and we will teach it to you. In your first few months you will get close review and clear guidance while you learn how we work. You will also join at a good time: the team is growing, new roles are being added, and we are underwriting a new product, so there is real room to learn, ask questions, and grow with us.



Success here means accurate work. The team trusts your numbers, your flags are clear, and any mistake you make happens once, not twice.



What Might Your Day Look Like

Your morning starts with a new deal from one of our business development colleagues. You go through the model piece by piece: the start date, the budget, the rent and revenue share assumptions, the cash flows, the IRR, and the margin the location is expected to earn per rentable square foot. The returns look fine at first, but pricing is tighter than it seems, so you note it clearly with the number that would need to change.



Late morning, updated figures arrive from Design and Construction. You check that they have flowed into the model correctly. One CapEx figure does not match the construction budget, so you confirm the right number with the construction team before it goes any further.



In the afternoon, you walk your business development colleague through the deal: what the returns look like, where the risk sits, and which assumptions matter most. They decide what happens next. Then priorities shift, and another colleague needs support on a deal heading to Investment Committee, so you move over and check that every figure in the review material ties back to the underwriting.



Before you wrap up, you update your trackers and checklists so the team knows where every deal you are supporting stands.



What You Will Own

 - Underwrite assigned deals in Excel, checking every assumption and making sure each component, from start date and budgets to pricing and IRR, tracks.
 - Explain each deal's returns clearly, including IRR, cash flows, P&L, and margin, so business development can make an informed decision.
 - Flag where a deal is tight, on pricing, occupancy, CapEx, OpEx, rent, or revenue share, and where it may need more support.
 - Make sure figures from Design, Construction, and Finance carry through accurately into the deal.
 - Support deal reviews and Investment Committee materials with numbers that hold up to scrutiny.
 - Support several business development colleagues across their deal flow, moving between priorities as needs change.
 - Keep the trackers and checklists that help the team stay accurate as deal volume grows.
You Will Love This Role If...
 - You are curious about real estate and want to understand why a deal works, not just what the model says.
 [...]  - Nice to have: exposure to leases, landlords, or office and flexible workspace, and progress toward a designation such as the CFA or CPA. You do not need Argus or prior knowledge of our underwriting approach.

- 3–5 years of experience in mortgage pricing, secondary marketing, capital markets analytics, FP&A, or a similar quantitative role at a lender or investor

title: AI Finance Researcher (MBA Student)
description:
AI FINANCE RESEARCHER (MBA STUDENT)




ABOUT THE ROLE

AI systems are becoming increasingly capable of building financial models, analyzing business performance, and generating investment research. Yet complex financial decisions still demand the experience, critical thinking, and professional judgment of seasoned finance experts.

At Julius Research, we're recruiting exceptional MBA students with professional experience in Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A), Investment Banking (IB), Private Equity (PE), Venture Capital (VC), Hedge Funds, Corporate Finance, Asset Management, or Equity Research.

Your primary responsibility will be to create sophisticated financial challenges that test the limits of frontier AI models.

Your work will expose weaknesses in today's leading AI systems and contribute to improving their financial reasoning capabilities.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Design expert-level financial research and analysis tasks inspired by real-world finance and investment workflows.

 - Create complex financial modeling challenges involving DCF valuations, LBOs, three-statement models, forecasting, budgeting, and scenario analysis.

 - Develop realistic FP&A problems involving revenue forecasting, budget variance analysis, cash flow planning, unit economics, and business performance evaluation.

 - Construct investment research scenarios involving M&A, company valuation, market analysis, investment due diligence, and capital allocation decisions.

 - Design multi-stage analytical problems that require interpreting incomplete data, reconciling conflicting information, and making defensible financial judgments.

 - Identify weaknesses in advanced AI models by evaluating their calculations, assumptions, analytical approaches, and financial conclusions.

 - Develop expert solutions, scoring criteria, and research benchmarks to measure AI performance.


REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Currently enrolled in a Top 25 MBA program (or recent graduate), preferably with a concentration in Finance, Investments, or Corporate Strategy.

 - 2+ years of professional experience in FP&A, Corporate Finance, Investment Banking, Private Equity, Venture Capital, Hedge Funds, Asset Management, Equity Research, or related finance roles.

 - Previous experience as an Investment Banking Analyst/Associate, Private Equity Associate, Venture Capital Associate, Investment Analyst, Equity Research Analyst, FP&A Analyst/Manager or Corporate Finance Analyst.

 - Strong understanding of financial statement analysis, financial modeling, forecasting, company valuation, or investment research.

 - Hands-on experience with one or more of the following:
   
   - Investment Banking & Private Equity: DCF valuation, LBO modeling, comparable company analysis, M&A, and transaction due diligence.
   
   - Venture Capital & Growth Equity: Startup valuation, financial projections, market sizing, unit economics, and investment underwriting.
   
   - Hedge Funds & Equity Research: Fundamental research, earnings analysis, financial forecasting, and investment thesis development.
   
   - Corporate Finance & FP&A: Budgeting, forecasting, variance analysis, financial planning, management reporting, and three-statement modeling.

 - Excellent quantitative reasoning, problem-solving, written communication, and attention to detail.


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Experience at a leading investment bank, private equity firm, venture capital fund, hedge fund, Fortune 500 finance team, or high-growth technology company.

 - Proficiency in Excel financial modeling and tools such as Capital IQ, Bloomberg, FactSet, PitchBook, or financial planning software.

 - Interest in artificial intelligence, large language models (LLMs), and AI applications in financial services.

description:
ABOUT US:

Camber builds software to improve the quality and accessibility of healthcare. We streamline and replace manual work so clinicians can focus on what they do best: providing great care. For more details on our thesis, check out our write-up: What is Camber? https://camberhealth.notion.site/What-is-Camber-1a6c4e2fa5318049b6beef91b8ed7d1a?pvs=4

We’ve raised $50M in funding from phenomenal supporters at a16z, Craft Ventures, YCombinator, Manresa, and many others who are committed to improving the accessibility of care. For more information, take a look at: Announcing Camber https://www.camber.health/knowledge/launch


ABOUT OUR CULTURE:

Our mission to change behavioral health starts with us and how we operate. We don’t want to just change behavioral health, we want to change the way startups operate. Here are a few tactical examples:

1) Improving accessibility and quality of healthcare is something we live and breathe. Everyone on Camber’s team cares deeply about helping clinicians and patients.

2) We have to have a sense of humor. Healthcare is so broken, it's depressing if you don't laugh with us.


ABOUT THE ROLE

Camber is hiring an Enterprise Strategy Associate to partner with our Director of Enterprise Revenue to build the narrative behind our largest client partnerships. Revenue cycle is the bloodline of a clinic, and through data, you build trust with the client. You will drive the narrative that helps a clinic understand the impact Camber can have on its business, and you’ll use it to shape the strategy of the deal.

This is not a traditional analyst role. You will follow a clinic through its entire time at Camber, from the first conversation to a fully rolled-out partnership, and keep driving the value of Camber at every step. You will join a team that values agency, intellectual honesty, and a “rowing in the same direction” mentality.

Your time will be split across three stages of the client journey:

 - Go-to-Market: You leverage a clinic’s data to build the narrative for how Camber can impact its revenue cycle, partnering with a Director of Enterprise Revenue on the analysis and story to win the deal.

 - Implementation: You are the subject-matter expert on both Camber and the clinic, and that expertise drives how we serve them. You help make sure the value of Camber is seen and understood as we roll out.

 - Stable State: You work with the strategic account management team to inform and prepare material for the clinic’s key decision-makers to help them understand the impact Camber is having on their business.


WHAT YOU’LL DO


BE THE ANALYTICAL AND NARRATIVE BACKBONE OF THE DEAL

 - Run Diagnostics: Dig into a clinic’s billing, claims, and payment data to find where revenue is being left on the table (e.g., denial trends, underpayments, aging AR, payer-specific patterns).

 - Build the Business Case: Size the opportunity in dollars and collection rate points, and build the ROI models that decision-makers use to say yes.

 - Drive the Strategy of the Deal: Use what the data says to decide where the deal goes: which problems to lead with, what each stakeholder cares about, and what a pilot needs to prove.

 - Build Executive-Ready Materials: Turn analysis into crisp, top-down stories that client leaders can act on and take to their own leadership.


IDENTIFY WHAT REALLY MATTERS

 - Ready the Internal Team: Surface what a new enterprise account or vertical will demand (e.g., net-new integrations, custom analyses, reporting needs) and get Product, Engineering, Data, and Operations ahead of it before go-live.

 - Flag Early: Act as the account’s early-warning system. When something in the data or the relationship looks off, raise it to the right people before it becomes a fire.


ANCHOR THE CLIENT ON CAMBER’S IMPACT

 - Own the Data Relationship: Be the go-to partner for the client’s data and analytics leads through the pilot and beyond.

 - Prove and Communicate Value: Track performance against the baseline and tell the story of Camber’s impact in recurring business reviews. Delivering results is half the job. Making sure the client knows about them is the other half.
WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR
 - Experience: 1–3 years in management consulting, investment banking, or strategy at a fast-moving startup.
 - Data Fluency: Experience working with large, messy data sets and turning them into conclusions that drive decisions.
 - Customer and Executive Exposure: Previous experience working directly with customers and senior executives.
 - Commercial Instinct: You understand how businesses make money and what motivates the people making the decision, and you can tie your analysis back to both.
 - Learning Velocity: Healthcare or RCM experience is a plus but not required. What matters more is that you do your homework, ask sharp questions, and ramp quickly into a complex domain.
WHAT YOU BRING
 - The ability to turn analysis into a narrative that moves a decision, not just a data dump.
 - “Client hands”: you’re comfortable and credible in front of a client, and you can hold your ground when the room pushes back.

 Discover your opportunity with Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group (MUFG), one of the world’s leading financial groups. Across the globe, we’re 150,000 colleagues, striving to make a difference for every client, organization, and community we serve. We stand for our values, building long-term relationships, serving society, and fostering shared and sustainable growth for a better world.
 With a vision to be the world’s most trusted financial group, it’s part of our culture to put people first, listen to new and diverse ideas and collaborate toward greater innovation, speed and agility. This means investing in talent, technologies, and tools that empower you to own your career.
 Join MUFG, where being inspired is expected and making a meaningful impact is rewarded.
The selected colleague will work at an MUFG office or client sites four days per week and work remotely one day. A member of our recruitment team will provide more details. 
 Job Summary: 
 We're seeking an Associate to join our growing Portfolio Management Group. You will conduct credit analysis and recommendation for financial institution credits across the spectrum of FIG portfolio:
- Banks / Business Development Companies / Asset Managers / Insurance companies (Life & Health insurance and Property & Casualty companies)
- Structured financial solutions
- Asset based lending including Fund and NAV lending
 You will prepare and evaluate credit proposals and make recommendations to management on credit approval. You’ll be also monitoring the client financial, industry and credit trends regularly.
 Responsibilities: 
- Perform due diligence on new transactions as well as regularly scheduled evaluation of the existing loan portfolio.
- Coordinate and communicate account information across various constituencies throughout the organization.
- Responsible for knowledge of particular industries and all current events in assigned portfolio utilizing internal and external sources.
- Oversee covenants compliance database and facility closing due diligence, including documentation.
- Attend client meetings.
- Participate in special projects as assigned.
 Advanced Credit/Underwriting Solutions: 
- Work within a deal team environment (with Global Relationship Managers, Credit Administration, Sponsor Coverage, and Capital Markets) to support the development and analysis of financing structures/strategies.
- Prescreen proposed transactions to identify critical structural issues and risks, balancing institutional policy with business development needs.
- Support credit analysis for structured credit transactions (derivatives transactions, receivable securitizations).
- Understand and maintain knowledge of industries represented in portfolio, including technical aspects and regulatory issues.
- Conduct site visits and participate in client and bank meetings.
 Policy and Deal Advocacy: 
- Support the communication with the credit approval division including final hold level strategies to ensure alignment of risk strategy and policy.
- Evaluate and establish appropriate ratings for transactions and correlate appropriate exposure level with regard to exposure on both a transaction and group level.
- Ensure compliance with policy and regulatory requirements.

- Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business or Economics (CFA or MBA is a plus).

- Insurance companies including property casualty companies and life insurance with preferred experience in life insurance and side car credit terms negotiation

- Hanwha Renewables – specializing in utility-scale solar and battery energy storage systems (BESS)
- Chariot Energy – providing retail electricity services for residential, commercial, and industrial customers in deregulated markets

Working closely with the team head, this role will coordinate day-to-day project activities, track deliverables, and support business planning, budgeting, and management reporting.

- Prepare management reporting: Draft concise presentations and project updates covering progress, budgets, risks, next steps, and decisions required. Check supporting information for accuracy and consistency.

- Support transaction readiness: Coordinate document requests, data-room updates, and due diligence schedules with development, finance, and legal teams.
 REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS 
- 2–4 years of relevant experience in project coordination, business planning, consulting, or a related role.
- Experience coordinating assignments involving multiple teams and following deliverables through to completion.
- Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and the ability to manage competing deadlines.
- Ability to turn complex information into clear written summaries, presentations, and actionable next steps.
- Proficiency in Excel and PowerPoint, with the ability to organize data and perform basic financial analysis.
 Preferred Qualifications 
- Experience in energy, data centers, infrastructure, or another project-based business.
- Familiarity with project budgets, development milestones, and financial concepts such as capital expenditure, operating costs, and cash flow.
- Experience working across business units or supporting management reporting and internal approval processes.
 COMPENSATION: $130,000 - $145,000 salary

 Capacity Planning Consultant 
 This role can be done in office or remotely 
 The capacity Planning Consultant is accountable for the development and maintenance of comprehensive staffing models supporting Operations Service/Call Centers. The models determine resource (staff) requirements for workload demands for long term planning. The models contemplate business processes, staff productivity, timeliness, growth, invest initiatives, transfer of work, as well as turnover and hiring.
 The position works very closely with other members of the Operations and Finance teams and is critical in the development of annual operating plan/budget and regular outlooks.
 • Development and maintenance of Operations Service/Call Center staff models • Identify and detail hiring, schedule, development time and skilling recommendations
 • Variance and scenario analysis
 RESPONSIBILITIES 
 • Act as liaison between Operations, Training, HR, Finance and Expense business partners with regards to staffing and capacity planning. Develop and maintain strong working relationships with partners.
 • Establish staff plans and/or capacity requirements based on data and analytics. Maintain comprehensive knowledge of staffing model inputs and methodology. Work closely with Operations business partners in the development of work process time standards.
 • Conduct planning meetings to discuss and or communicate capacity needs, risks, opportunities and results to various functions.
 • Conduct detailed variance analytics and identify key business drivers of change. Research, forecast and report on demand drivers. Review forecast for accuracy and make proactive changes to minimize variances.
 • Influence and negotiate with business partners and colleagues. Clearly articulate points of view and provide compelling rationale to influence decisions.
 • Working closely with the Operational Lines Finance, Expense and Operations leads, identify trends, quantify impacts, and communicate business results relative to staffing implications on a monthly basis. Respond to “what-if” scenarios, cost benefit requests, and other projects that have staffing implications. Able to quantify implications of initiatives on staffing needs.

 • Develop benchmarking metrics in order to understand efficiency/productivity of actual planned staffing levels. Assess risk and opportunities.
 • Develop and maintain expertise in business process. Be able to translate into working staff model that allows the isolation of impacts of change in variables. • Participate in model optimization techniques that drive efficiency and optimize resource utilization.
 • Play a key role in the financial outlook and operating plan process by submitting staffing projections for current and outer years. Communicate detailed explanations of change drivers and gain approval from leadership on an ongoing basis.
 QUALIFICATIONS 
 • Experience in building capacity plans for both call center and back office operations
 • Long term workforce modeling, building and maintenance
 • Long term Forecasting experience looking out at least 2 years
 • Service Operations/Contact Center and/or business forecasting experience
 • Experience in constructing quantitative analysis
 • Bachelor’s Degree preferred
 • Strong quantitative and mathematical skills
 • Possesses strong to advanced MS EXCEL skills.
 • Familiarity with IEX and workforce planning tools
 • Adept in data mining, data analysis, and data presentation.

 Sparkfund prices and structures its Distributed Capacity Procurement deals using a set of programmatic pricing models, and this role is responsible for both sides of that work: building the ad hoc project finance models a deal needs when it falls outside the existing templates, and keeping the standing programmatic models accurate as cost, revenue, timing, and financing assumptions shift.  Nice to Have

- Experience in infrastructure, energy, or utility-facing businesses

ABOUT THE TEAM
