WHAT YOU'LL DO

Our financial models have two audiences. Internally, they guide how we plan, hire, and raise capital. Externally, they help a large veterinary network decide whether to partner with us, and the EBITDA lift model and pricing proposal are often what a network's CFO evaluates before signing. You will spend about 70% of your time on FP&A and about 30% on customer-facing modeling. The work rewards people who ask why a number is what it is, can turn a vague question into a structured analysis, and care whether the reader understands the answer. After a year, you will own the operating model, the board package, and the standard enterprise proposal model, and the sales team will bring you into late-stage deals as a matter of course.




RESPONSIBILITIES

FP&A (about 70%)

 - Prepare the monthly management report and the board package.

 - Track unit economics by segment and by hospital, including acquisition cost, lifetime value, gross margin, and contribution margin.

 - Build investor-ready models, scenario analyses, and data room materials during fundraising.

 - Build and maintain management reporting and self-service dashboards in Sigma.

Customer-facing modeling (about 30%)

 - Maintain the EBITDA lift model and unit economics framework we present to enterprise prospects.

 - Model custom proposals across adoption levels, plan designs, fee structures, and rebates, showing the effect on both the customer's economics and Nest's margins.

 - Model revenue recognition for enterprise customers under ASC 606, including allocation, consumption-based recognition, straight-line amortization, and breakage.

 - Join customer calls when a CFO or procurement team wants to test assumptions on incrementality and ROI.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Experience with Sigma, Looker, Tableau, or a similar BI tool.

 - Working knowledge of ASC 606 and subscription billing.

 2. Target and quota setting

You will work closely with Sales, Customer Success, Finance, People, and other RevOps teammates to turn business objectives into clear targets, reliable incentive processes, and actionable performance insights.

Footprint is the agentic platform that learns your compliance program and runs it end to end.


Compliance teams at banks and fintechs are drowning in financial crimes investigations. Transaction volumes are surging, regulators keep raising the bar, and the work still runs on manual review queues stitched together from legacy vendors. The people at UiPath believe in the transformative power of automation to change how the world works. We’re committed to creating category-leading enterprise software that unleashes that power.

To make that happen, we need people who are curious, self-propelled, generous, and genuine. People who love being part of a fast-moving, fast-thinking growth company. And people who care—about each other, about UiPath, and about our larger purpose.

Could that be you?




ABOUT THE ROLE:



We are seeking a highly analytical, results-driven Senior FP&A Analyst to join our Corporate FP&A team. This role sits at the intersection of financial planning, investor relations analytics, and strategic finance, with direct exposure to M&A evaluation, capital markets communications, and top-line performance modeling for a public SaaS company. You will work closely with senior leadership and the CFO's office to shape how the company communicates its financial story to the Street, the Board, and prospective transaction counterparties.




WHAT YOU WILL DO AT UIPATH:



• Help design and maintain a long-term financial model projecting UiPath's future

fiscal year top-line metrics, including ARR movements such as new business,

expansion, contraction, and churn, with sensitivity analysis suitable for board and

investor scenarios.

• Build and refine SaaS valuation and benchmarking frameworks (ARR growth,

NRR/DBNRR, Rule of 40, magic number, CAC/LTV) to support investor relations

messaging and peer comparisons against public SaaS and enterprise software

comparables.

• Support M&A activity including target screening, financial due diligence,

accretion/dilution and synergy modeling, and integration of acquired ARR and

revenue streams into consolidated top-line forecasts.

• Create and implement innovative forecasting methodologies across a variety of top-

line models, adaptable to inorganic growth scenarios and changes in business mix.

• Analyze KPIs related to product and sales performance, developing new analyses to

assess business health and translate operating metrics into the language used by

equity analysts and institutional investors.

• Prepare board decks, earnings materials, and investor relations presentations,

working with IR and the CFO to ensure numbers translate cleanly into external

narrative on a monthly and quarterly cadence.

• Own quality assurance on all board-level and external financial communications,

ensuring consistency between internal models, public disclosures, and any

transaction-related materials.

• Partner cross-functionally with Corporate Development, Treasury, and Legal on

deal-related financial analysis as M&A opportunities arise.





WHAT YOU WILL BRING TO THE TEAM:



• Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Business, Economics, or related field; 2-

4 years of relevant experience in FP&A, investment banking, equity research,

corporate development, or transaction advisory.

• Strong financial modeling skills, including exposure to SaaS metrics (ARR,

NRR/DBNRR, billings, FCF) and M&A analysis (valuation, accretion/dilution, synergy

modeling) a plus.

• Mastery of MS Office (Excel, PowerPoint), with demonstrated ability to build

complex, audit-ready financial models under tight deadlines.

• Strong written and oral communication skills, with the ability to translate

quantitative analysis into clear, board- and investor-ready narrative.

• Organized, analytical, motivated, curious, resourceful, flexible, and collaborative,

with the judgment to handle market-sensitive and confidential information.

• A self-starter with a proactive attitude who seeks out opportunities for themselves

and the team.

• Strong project and time management skills, comfortable operating in a fast-paced,

deadline-driven, publicly-traded company environment.

Arca is a wealth management firm built from the ground up with AI. The kind of service that used to require a team of specialists behind you, the kind that makes you feel like the only person in the room, should be available to far more than the ultra-wealthy.

Underneath, it keeps a living understanding of each client. It remembers the thing you mentioned once, six months ago. It notices when your life changes — a new job, a new kid, a market shift — and adjusts before you think to ask. You won't see the technology. You'll just notice your advisor seems to know you better than any financial professional ever has.



That's the product we're growing: client by client, on the strength of the experience itself. We started by acquiring firms managing over $1B in client assets, which gave us real advisors, real clients, and real financial outcomes to build against from day one. title: Pricing & Monetization Analyst
description:
About Bask Health
 Bask Health is a telehealth technology platform that helps entrepreneurs, healthcare businesses, and brands launch, manage, and grow their own telehealth businesses.
 Our platform brings together storefronts, patient experiences, clinical workflows, pharmacy operations, and business management tools in one place.
 We help businesses operate their own healthcare brands without having to build all the technology and operational infrastructure themselves.
 We're a fast-moving team that values initiative, ownership, and clear communication. Our teams collaborate across Finance, Product, Engineering, Sales, Customer Success, and Operations to improve how our platform works and support the businesses that rely on it.
 About the Role
 We're looking for a Pricing & Monetization Analyst to help Bask Health evaluate how we price our platform and services, identify revenue opportunities, and develop pricing models that support long-term growth.
 You'll analyze merchant activity, product usage, transaction volume, pricing structures, and costs to understand how different monetization approaches affect revenue and profitability.
 This role combines financial analysis, product economics, and commercial strategy. You'll build models to evaluate pricing changes, compare monetization scenarios, and work with internal teams to understand the potential impact of new or updated pricing structures.
 You'll also help monitor the performance of existing pricing models and identify opportunities to improve how Bask captures value from the services we provide.
 We're looking for someone who enjoys working with data, understanding how businesses generate revenue, and developing practical recommendations based on financial analysis.
 What You'll Do
- Analyze existing platform and service pricing structures to understand revenue performance.
- Build financial models to evaluate pricing and monetization opportunities.
- Assess how merchant usage, transaction volume, and product mix affect revenue and margins.
- Evaluate potential changes to subscription fees, transaction-based pricing, service fees, or other applicable commercial models.
- Compare alternative pricing scenarios and estimate their financial impact.
- Identify opportunities to improve monetization while maintaining competitive merchant value.
- Analyze product-level and service-level economics to support pricing decisions.
- Partner with Finance to validate revenue, cost, and profitability assumptions.
- Collaborate with Product to understand how new features or services may affect monetization.
- Support evaluations of pricing structures for new products and platform capabilities.
- Analyze how pricing changes may affect different merchant segments.
- Review merchant spending patterns and identify opportunities for pricing improvements.
- Develop reports and dashboards that monitor pricing and monetization performance.
- Evaluate the results of implemented pricing changes.
- Analyze relationships between platform usage, pricing, and realized revenue.
- Support commercial teams with pricing comparisons and financial recommendations.
- Identify inconsistencies in pricing structures and recommend improvements.
- Evaluate the financial trade-offs of discounts, incentives, and nonstandard commercial arrangements.
- Research relevant market pricing approaches and competitive monetization models.
- Work with Customer Success to understand merchant feedback related to pricing and perceived value.

description:
About us:

Jerry.ai http://Jerry.ai is a Series C, YC-backed tech startup with 5M+ customers and $240M in funding. Founded in 2017, product launched in 2019, and achieved profitability in 2024.

 

Why we exist:

Your car, home, and motorcycle aren't just purchases, they're the physical embodiment of the life you've worked hard to build. Yet the experience of owning them is stuck in the 90s. Every step of the journey — buying, insuring, maintaining, repairing, selling — is fragmented, complicated, and expensive.

 

Imagine having a trusted friend in your pocket who takes care of everything: they find you the right car or home at the right price, lock in the best insurance rate without you lifting a finger, remind you before that service appointment turns into an expensive repair, and help you sell at the best price when the time is right. That friend is Jerry.

 

We are building the first AI-powered advisor to manage all your physical assets. We started with your car in 2019, now we’re expanding into new verticals (e.g. home, motorcycle, RV, boat).

 

Why We’re Hiring

Our Business Operations & Analytics  team has been a force multiplier and accelerant to our business that has helped us reach these pivotal milestones in spite of headwinds and within a highly competitive market. They are a team of former McKinsey, BCG and Bain consultants who drive data & insights, and inform decision-making across every corner of our business. They are analytical powerhouses and first principles problem solvers who push forward our most important initiatives across product, growth, tech, and operations.

 

Every business unit has a Business Operations & Analytics team member embedded within it  —  someone who doesn't just run analyses and build dashboards, but shapes what questions we should ask, what data to pull, what conclusions to draw, what decisions to make, and then drives our teams towards our next goal: go from 5M to 50M customers and become a $10B business in the next 4 years. 

 

As our business continues to expand, there is growing demand for more Business Operations & Analytics team members. We are hiring 2-3 people to drive impact in these areas:

 - Growth Marketing 

 - Product Development

 - Strategic Partnerships 

 

On leveling: You may see job ads for this role at different job levels. Our priority is finding the right people, we can be flexible with job title/leveling.

 

Why You Will (Or Won't) Like Working Here

 - No slides: If you've worked in consulting, you know what it feels like to be up at 3am reformatting a deck. That doesn't exist here. The only work that gets done at Jerry is work that will materially change the trajectory of our business — an important product, a new growth channel, a key metric, a critical partner relationship, etc. 

 - No corporate fluff: The Business Operations & Analytics team is 14 insatiable learners who care deeply about solving difficult problems and making a tangible impact. Every person owns a critical domain. There is no bloat, unnecessary meetings, or waiting for approvals. 

 - Hands-on: This is not a pure strategy role, you will also own execution. Your day-to-day will be surfacing analytical insights, driving decisions, and seeing them through end-to-end. 

 

What You'll Own

You'll sit on our central Business Operations & Analytics team but you’ll be embedded in one of Jerry's core business areas — growth, product, AI and automation, strategic partnerships — and own the analytical function for that business unit end-to-end.

 - Define the right problems: Before any analysis, understand what business question it's answering and what decision it will inform. Push back if the question is flawed.

 - Data and insights: Define metrics, build reports, run analyses, design experiments, and surface data insights that move your team's key metrics.

 - Drive outcomes: Bring recommendations to your counterparts in product, growth, finance or operations, tell them what's happening and why, and what next steps should be.
Who You Are
 - First principles thinker: You break ambiguous problems into clear hypotheses before touching data. You're analytically strong (comfortable with SQL or Python) but your instinct is to ask "what are we trying to solve here?" before jumping to "what should I build?" 
 - Direct communicator: You can walk a skeptical stakeholder through a complex finding and get buy-in quickly. You write clearly, speak precisely, and don't bury the lede.
 - Owner: You act like your name is on the door. If something is broken, you feel responsible for fixing it, even if it’s outside of your swim lane.
What You'll Bring
 - 2+ years of experience at a consulting firm, investment bank, or high-growth technology company.
 - Strong analytical skills; ability to pull, structure, and interpret data independently.
 - Track record of owning ambiguous problems and delivering impact.
 - Clear, persuasive communicator who can influence decisions at the leadership level.
Our Tools
SQL (Clickhouse), Metabase, Python, Jupyter Hub, GitHub.
While we appreciate your interest and application, due to the volume of applications we receive, only applicants under consideration will be contacted.

title: Retail Operations Analyst
location: Santa Ana, California, United States; Remote
description:
Location: Remote (United States, Pacific Time hours). Orange County, CA preferred.
 Type: Full-Time
 Salary: $75,000 – $90,000 base, depending on experience
 About Us
 eJam is a bootstrapped consumer products company that has built, scaled, and exited multiple brands — all without ever taking a dollar of outside capital. Our portfolio includes category leaders ranked at the top of Amazon, carried in major retailers nationwide, and sold across DTC, marketplaces, and every channel in between.
 We’re not a startup hoping something works. We’re a team that has done it repeatedly — taken products from idea to category leader, landed them on retail shelves nationwide, and built real brands that consumers love. We operate like a holding company with the speed of a startup: small team, no bureaucracy, massive ownership.
 This is the place where you’ll see the entire machine — sourcing, product development, packaging, manufacturing, compliance, marketing, marketplace strategy, retail — all under one roof. If you want to learn how consumer products actually get built and shipped at scale, there is no faster education than this.
 The Role
 You will be the person who knows, every week, how eJam products are selling on the shelf and online at Target, Walmart, Kroger, QVC and the accounts we add next. Growth comes from reach, so you turn retailer point of sale, inventory and syndicated data into the in stock, replenishment and sell through decisions that keep us on shelf and growing.
 You own the retailer portals and item data, the weekly performance package, trade spend and deductions to the penny, and the operating rhythm between Sales, Supply Chain, Marketing and Finance that makes retail profitable, not just present.
 Mission: Finance and the brand leads know which SKU is winning at which retailer, what it costs to be there, and what to ship next, before they have to ask.
 What You'll Own
 Sell through and retailer data 
- Pull and analyze POS, inventory, in stock and replenishment data from retailer portals (Walmart Retail Link and Supplier One, Target Partners Online, Kroger and QVC reporting) every week
- Build and maintain the weekly retail performance package by account and SKU: velocity, distribution and ACV, in stocks, on time in full, promotional lift and plan vs actual
- Read syndicated and panel data (NielsenIQ, Circana, Numerator, 84.51) to size category trends, competitive shelf position and household penetration gaps
- Maintain the retail dashboard in BigQuery with the data team so retail sell in, sell through and competitor views stay current
 Forecasting, inventory and item management 
- Work with Supply Chain and Cin7 on retail demand forecasts, purchase order planning, item setup and attributes, new item launches and SKU transitions across stores and .com
- Flag out of stock and overstock risk by account before it costs a facing, and recommend replenishment and allocation moves
 Trade, deductions and profitability 
- Track trade spend, promotions, chargebacks and deductions by retailer, validate them against agreements and work with Finance to dispute what is wrong and accrue what is right
- Build the retail profitability view by account and SKU, gross to net through trade, freight and fees to contribution, and feed it into budget and forecast
 Account rhythm 
- Line review, joint business planning and buyer meeting materials with the Sales lead, and the retailer documentation, scorecards and communications that keep every account organized
- Retail operating SOPs, with recurring reporting automated with Claude and documented so it survives a vacation
 What Success Looks Like
- 30 days: access and data pulls are set up for every retailer portal and the weekly sell through package publishes for Target and Walmart
- 90 days: the deductions and trade spend log is current by retailer with open disputes filed, the retail profitability view exists by account and SKU, and a retail demand forecast is in place with Supply Chain for every active SKU
- 6 months: the retail dashboard ties to Finance's numbers, in stock rate and forecast accuracy are tracked and improving, deductions are being recovered, and the weekly package is what the buyers and the CEO both read
 Requirements 
 Required (all four, no exceptions) 
- Retailer data: pulled and analyzed POS, inventory and in stock data from Walmart Retail Link or Supplier One, Target Partners Online, Kroger or a comparable portal, on a weekly cadence
- Forecast and replenishment: built or supported a retail demand forecast, purchase order plan or open to buy with lead times and weeks of supply
- Retail gross to net: reconciled trade, promotions, chargebacks and deductions for a retailer, or built a retailer P&L, and can name the deductions that killed margin
- Syndicated data: read NielsenIQ, Circana, SPINS or Numerator to size velocity, distribution, penetration or promotional lift
 Also required

title: Business Operations Associate
description:
What is Coast 
 Coast is re-imagining the trillion-dollar U.S. B2B card payments infrastructure, with a focus on the country’s 500,000 commercial fleets, 40 million commercial vehicles, and many millions of commercial drivers. The incumbent technologies that cater to these customers are decades old, and businesses with fleets increasingly demand modern digital experiences and transparent financial services products. Coast’s mission is to deliver this at a transformational scale, beginning with the Coast Fleet and Fuel Card built on a cutting-edge spend management platform.
 About the Role 
 Coast’s biggest initiatives cross every team. You’ll own them: get the right people aligned, keep the work moving, and make sure it lands.
 As a Business Operations Associate, that someone is you. You’ll own and run cross-functional projects tied to Coast’s top priorities, from first scoping to final handoff. You’ll work with leaders across the company, so you’ll need to be credible with executives and just as comfortable in the details with the people doing the work.
 AI is a big part of how we do this. You’ll use it to plan faster, synthesize information, draft and analyze, and automate the repetitive parts of project work. You’ll also run projects that put AI to use across the business. You don’t need to be an engineer. You do need to be the person who reaches for AI first, and who can tell when it’s doing a good job and when it isn’t.
 This is a role for someone who gets energy from turning an ambiguous goal into a clear plan, getting a dozen people aligned, and shipping. You’ll be expected to act like an owner: you take responsibility for the outcome, not just your piece of it.
 It’s a generalist role with broad exposure to how a growth-stage fintech runs. Over time, you can build depth in an area you care about and take on bigger parts of the business as it scales.
 What You’ll Do 
 Own cross-functional projects end to end 
- Run company-level and cross-team initiatives from scoping through launch: define the goal, build the plan, line up owners, set milestones, and drive it to done.
- Keep projects moving across teams that don’t report to you. You get things unstuck by making the next step obvious and the tradeoffs clear.
- Spot risks and dependencies early, raise them with a recommendation, and keep leaders informed without making them chase you.
- Close projects properly: document what shipped, what you learned, and what happens next.
 Be the connective tissue across the company 
- Work with Product, Sales, Finance, Risk, Legal, People, and Operations to make sure the right people are in the room and decisions get made.
- Translate between teams. Take a goal from an executive and break it into work others can act on, and take messy ground-level input and turn it into something leadership can decide on.
- Run the cadences that keep cross-functional work on track: kickoffs, standups, status updates, and retros.
- Support quarterly planning and goal tracking by turning priorities into projects with owners and dates.
 Help figure out what we should do next 
- Scope and evaluate new opportunities, such as a new process, partnership, or initiative, and bring leaders a clear recommendation backed by the numbers.
- Build the analyses and decision frameworks that help leadership prioritize and decide where to put time and money.
- Take ideas from “this could work” to a pilot, then to something the company runs.
 Use AI to move faster and to help the company use it 
- Use AI in your own project work: planning, synthesizing inputs from many teams, drafting, analysis, and status reporting. Build repeatable workflows and prompts that cut the manual work out of running a project.

title: Economist, Macro & Economic Insights

description:
We believe that the way people interact with their finances will drastically improve in the next few years. We’re dedicated to empowering this transformation by building the tools and experiences that thousands of developers use to create their own products. Plaid powers the tools millions of people rely on to live a healthier financial life. We work with thousands of companies like Venmo, SoFi, several of the Fortune 500, and many of the largest banks to make it easy for people to connect their financial accounts to the apps and services they want to use. Plaid’s network covers 12,000 financial institutions across the US, Canada, UK and Europe. Founded in 2013, the company is headquartered in San Francisco with offices in New York, Seattle, Washington D.C., Raleigh, London, and Amsterdam.



The Economics Team uses economic research and data science to deepen our understanding of economic, credit, and financial trends. We combine rigorous empirical analysis with clear communication to inform decisions across and beyond Plaid.



You will conduct applied economic research, develop reliable analytical methods, and turn complex findings into clear, useful insights. Working with economists and data scientists, you will own research projects from question framing and data preparation through validation and written communication. This is a hands-on role for an economist who enjoys working with large datasets, exercising sound judgment, and explaining evidence and limitations to a range of audiences. You will have opportunities to develop a research specialty and take on broader ownership as the team grows.



We're guided by our principles including impact, growing together, embracing openness and positivity, and inventing tomorrow; we're looking for leaders who are motivated by those same principles






Responsibilities

 - Investigating economic questions and trends through rigorous empirical research, from framing the question through analysis, validation, and communication

 - Working with large, complex datasets to develop reliable measures and reproducible analytical workflows

 - Evaluating findings against established research and public benchmarks, assessing data quality and representativeness, and clearly communicating uncertainty and limitations

 - Applying econometric and time-series methods to test hypotheses, assess robustness, and distinguish meaningful patterns from noise

 - Writing clear research briefs and presenting findings to technical and nontechnical audiences; partnering with colleagues across research, data science, and the business to identify useful questions and inform decisions






Qualifications

 Corporate Title: Associate

 Overview 
 Group Strategic Analytics (GSA) brings together Deutsche Bank’s quantitative modelling and analytics expertise across businesses. The team develops and delivers strategic analytics, pricing, risk, and P&L capabilities used across the Bank’s trading businesses.

You will develop quantitative analytics and market data capabilities supporting Fixed Income trading, with particular focus on interest rates products, curves, volatility, pricing, risk, and P&L.This is a highly quantitative, hands-on role offering exposure to the trading desk and the opportunity to combine financial modelling, software development, and markets knowledge to solve real-time business problems.

title: Clinical Research Associate II - FSP
description:
Precision for Medicine is not your typical CRO. We are passionate about supporting professional growth and are proud to share extremely high CRA retention rates compared to industry averages.
 CRAs join us, love their jobs, and stay because of the amazing people and enjoyable quality of life. Travel is reasonable and your work/life balance will benefit as a result. Most meaningfully - your voice will be heard. Working in a midsized CRO allows you to have influence and impact when it matters most with support from direct line management.
 To support continued growth from our clients, we are hiring all levels of CRAs experienced in monitoring Oncology, Cardiology, or Lupus,
 Position Summary: 
 The CRA II is a seasoned, experienced professional in monitoring and site management. Responsibilities will be dependent upon the type and timing of the program to which the CRA II is assigned and typically include activities involving start-up and study implementation, on-site monitoring of clinical research studies as well as on-going site management. Incumbents work independently as a study team member.
 Essential functions of the job include but are not limited to: 
- Oversees all aspects of study site management to ensure patient safety is protected, quality of data generated by managed sites resulting in consistently low query levels and in acceptable Quality Assurance reports.
- Provides guidance at the site and project level towards audit readiness standards and supports preparation for audit and required follow-up actions.
- Updates, tracks and maintains study specific trial management tools/systems, and status reports.
- If required, manages site start up procedures including the feasibility and recruitment of potential investigators, preparation of EC/IRB submissions, collection and review of regulatory documents, review and adaptation in Patient Informed Consents, notifications to IRB, EC and regulatory authorities, as appropriate, translation of study related documentation, organization of meetings and other tasks as instructed by the Clinical Trial Manager/Project Manager.
- If required, assists the negotiation of study budgets and the execution of investigator contracts under directions of Site Contract Management department/designee.
- Verifies the process of obtaining informed consent has been adequately performed and documented for each subject/patient, as required/appropriate. Assesses factors that might affect subject/patient’s safety and clinical data integrity at an investigator/physician site such as protocol deviation/violations and pharmacovigilance issues.
- Independently conducts all forms of site visits, including pre-study/ qualification, initiation, routine monitoring, and close-out visits, in accordance with the protocol, local laws, ICH-GCP and Precision SOPs. Prepares and submits for review, accurate and timely monitoring reports from all site visits (on-site and remote).
- Documents activities via confirmation letters, follow-up letters, trip reports, communication logs, and other required project documents as per SOPs, Clinical Monitoring Plan/Site Management Plan and client requirements. Supports subject/patient recruitment, retention and awareness strategies. Enters data into tracking systems as required to track all observations, ongoing status and assigned action items to resolution.
- Routinely reviews the Investigator Site File (ISF) for accuracy, timeliness and completeness. Reconciles contents of the ISF with the Trial Master File (TMF). Ensures the investigator/physician site is aware of the requirement of archiving essential documents in accordance with local guidelines and regulations.
- Communicates effectively and proactively with both site personnel and Precision Project and Clinical Trial Management to relay protocol/study issues including any deviations and implements necessary actions in response to those issues.
- Develops and maintains good working relationship with investigators and study staff, serving as an ambassador to promote Precision high quality and professional image.
 [...] - Performs data review activities, including remote EDC CRF and patient profiles review, query resolution, and assists data management and clinical data quality personnel to resolve data discrepancies.
 [...] - Prepares for and attends Investigator Meetings and/or sponsor face-to-face meetings. Participates in global clinical monitoring/project staff meetings (inclusive of Sponsor representation, as applicable) and attends clinical training sessions according to the project specific requirements.
 [...]  Qualifications: 
 Minimum Required: 
- 4-year college degree or equivalent experience in a scientific or healthcare discipline. 
- Two (2) years or more as a CRA in a CRO or equivalent, relevant experience and/or demonstrated competencies. Site management or equivalent experience 
in clinical research
 Other Required: 
- Excellent communication and organizational skills are essential. A team player.
- Evidence of a client focused approach
- Experience using computerized information systems, electronic spreadsheets, word processing and electronic mail.
- Ability to travel overnight. Up to 60% travel on average, based on regional requirements. International travel as needed.
- Fluency in English and for non-English speaking countries the local language of country where position based
 Preferred: 
- Graduate or postgraduate degree
- Lupus monitoring experience
- Experience monitoring in rare and complex therapeutic areas
- Experience monitoring EDC trials and EHR records
- Experience in biopharma or relevant therapeutic area
- Relevant site start-up (feasibility, contract negotiations, submissions) experience for the particular country
- Ability to monitor study sites, with supervision, according to protocol monitoring guidelines, SOPs, GCP and ICH guidelines.
 [...]

location: Hybrid (New York metro: New York City)
description:
About Us
 At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company.
 At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in.
 Available Locations: Austin, TX; San Francisco, CA; New York City 
 About the Team
 Our team researches web application attacks and turns that research into protections in Cloudflare’s Web Application Firewall (WAF). We build and maintain managed rules that help protect millions of Internet properties from known vulnerabilities, emerging exploits, and new attack techniques.
 We work at the intersection of vulnerability research, large-scale traffic analysis, and detection engineering. Using threat intelligence and telemetry from Cloudflare’s global network, we identify exploitation patterns, develop mitigations, and measure how well they work against real traffic. We partner with Engineering, Product, and customer-facing teams to improve coverage while minimizing false positives and disruption to legitimate applications.
 Who You Are
- You have hands-on experience in web application security, vulnerability research, or detection engineering, including writing and improving WAF rules, exploit signatures, or comparable detection logic.
- You understand HTTP/HTTPS, how web applications and proxies process requests, and common vulnerability classes such as SQL injection, cross-site scripting, remote code execution, SSRF, and insecure deserialization.
- You can analyze a vulnerability advisory or proof of concept, reproduce the exploit in a controlled environment, and identify the request characteristics that distinguish exploitation from legitimate traffic.
- You use SQL to investigate large datasets and a language such as Python, Go, or Rust to build research tools, automate analysis, and validate detections.
- You make evidence-based tradeoffs between detection coverage, false positives, and performance. You are comfortable investigating ambiguous reports and following issues through to resolution.
- You work effectively with engineers, product partners, and customer-facing teams, and communicate technical findings clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.
- You use AI fluently in research and coding workflows and have the judgment to know where it accelerates the work and where its outputs need independent validation.
- You are curious about how attackers exploit web applications and bypass defenses. You do not need to know our exact stack, but you should be eager to go deep in the domain.
 What You'll Do
 We are looking for a Security Research Analyst to research web application threats and develop the managed rules that protect Cloudflare customers. You will turn public CVEs, threat intelligence, customer reports, and internal telemetry into tested, effective mitigations.

title: Real Estate Market Intelligence Analyst
description:
MISSION

Neko Health is a health technology company that opened its first clinic in Stockholm in 2018, founded by Daniel Ek and Hjalmar Nilsonne.

In one hour, our scan combines radiation-free imaging, heart and circulation measurements, and same-visit blood results with time to talk it through with a clinician, so people can act on what matters before symptoms appear. We design and build our own hardware, software and clinical protocols, and more than 100,000 members have already had a scan, with 75% booking and prepaying their next one before they leave.

As a team, we chase 10X, not 10%, and we’re looking for people who think the same way to help us scale what we’ve started in Sweden, the UK, and now the US. Join the clinicians, engineers and business builders making prevention a routine part of care.


ROLE PURPOSE

Neko is opening clinics at pace: from a handful of US sites today to a 2028 cohort in the dozens and a portfolio in the hundreds by 2030. We are looking for a flexible, quantitative analyst to build the market intelligence behind that growth, using GIS, data, and analytics to decide where we open next, why, and how many clinics a market can support. The work runs from market sizing and member analytics through to site, market, and portfolio performance.

This is a build role. Neko is appointment-based, not footfall-driven, so the standard retail playbook does not transfer, and working out what predicts a successful clinic is the core problem. There is no framework to inherit: you will build the models and processes from scratch, and what you build in year one is what the whole portfolio runs on.

You will report to the Head of US Real Estate and work closely with the Transaction Managers, the Real Estate Associates, and our data analytics and engineering teams, in a small team where you help set the standard.




WHAT YOU'LL DELIVER IN THE FIRST 6-12 MONTHS

 - Market sizing: size the addressable member base by market and trade area, and translate it into how many clinics a market can support and in what order we should enter. This is the first priority of the role.

 - Site selection support: give Real Estate the analysis to justify new markets and infill locations, and to decide clinic sizing and spacing, including overlap and cannibalization as density increases.

 - Member data foundation: work with the internal data analytics and engineering teams to set up the full chain, from data collection to aggregation to analysis. Define our ideal member profile, find where those members live and work, and keep refining it as first-party data accumulates.

 - GIS platform, tool agnostic: use GrowthFactor today and own the catchment definitions, data layers, and scoring logic. Document the logic independently of the tool so it moves with us, and help evaluate and onboard the next platform when the time comes. Make the tool usable by Transaction Managers, not only by you.

 - Scoring and forecasting models: maintain a repeatable, defensible site scoring model and demand forecasts built to be re-run. A reforecast after a slipped opening or a shifted plan should be a scenario switch, not a rebuild.

 - Portfolio, market, and site performance: as clinics open, track and review performance at the portfolio, market, and site level. Compare forecast to actual, separate a bad site from a bad market from a bad launch, surface underperformers early, and document what each opening teaches us. Turn those learnings into updated site selection criteria, scoring weights, and sizing and spacing rules, so every new clinic is chosen with better information than the last.

 - Approval memos and cross-functional support: help produce LOI and Lease Approval Memos by coordinating inputs from Real Estate, Design, Construction, and Legal into a clear, one-page recommendation that leadership can decide from.

 - Process design and redesign: own the evaluation processes the team runs on, and version them. Retire what stops working, rebuild what needs it, and write it down so others can run it without you.
 [...] MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS
 - 3 to 6 years in real estate market analytics, site selection, location intelligence, data science, or strategy, ideally supporting multi-site physical expansion.
 - Hands-on GIS experience with GrowthFactor, Esri ArcGIS, Kalibrate, Buxton, SiteZeus, Placer, or similar. We care more that you understand catchment and scoring logic than that you know any one tool, because the tool will change.
 - Strong market sizing and quantitative skills: penetration and capture modeling, regression or other predictive approaches, and scenario and sensitivity analysis. Excel to a high standard.
 - Comfort with census, consumer spend, mobility, and first-party data, and honesty about the limits of each.
 - Financial literacy: you can build a basic site pro forma, calculate payback and break-even, and connect a demand forecast to a real estate decision.
 - Flexibility. You can tear down your own model without ego, rebuild it when the facts change, and stay organized while priorities shift.
 - Clear communication and intellectual honesty. You can defend an assumption to a skeptical executive in two minutes, name the two things most likely to be wrong, and say early when the data does not support the answer people want.
PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS
 - SQL or Python, which helps you work alongside engineers.
 - Specific, demonstrable use of AI to speed up analytical work, and real interest in teaching others to do the same.
 - Exposure to healthcare or regulated markets, or to European or multi-region expansion.
ABOUT TITLES AT NEKO
We use a simplified internal title framework that prioritises clarity over hierarchy, so the title on this posting may differ from your internal title. We’ll be open about the scope and level of the role throughout the process, so you know exactly what you’d be taking on.

Prime Intellect is building the open superintelligence stack: the infrastructure frontier AI labs build internally, made available to every ambitious AI team.

We are looking for people who want to build at the intersection of frontier research, real infrastructure, and go-to-market for a category that does not fully exist yet.


ROLE IMPACT

Quantitative finance is a demanding setting for agentic reinforcement learning: observations are noisy and non-stationary, actions have delayed and path-dependent consequences, naive objectives invite exploitation, and a convincing historical result can disappear under costs, constraints, or a new regime. You will build environments, evaluations, agents, and post-training methods for quantitative research and systematic decision-making. We have active programs with quantitative funds and other finance teams. The work may span research agents, market and portfolio simulators, time-series reasoning, execution, risk, and the production feedback loops that connect hypotheses to deployed systems.


RESPONSIBILITIES

Applied Research at Prime

We turn a workflow into tasks, environments, evaluations, and reward signals, run post-training experiments against real baselines, and deploy what works. When a result looks good, we find out whether the gain came from the model or from the data, harness, inference, or infrastructure. The reusable parts become shared research, open-source systems, and product capabilities.

Every Applied Research role is externally facing. Most researchers work directly with customers, users, or research partners while maintaining a substantive research agenda.

Representative early problems

 - Build a quantitative-research environment where an agent forms a hypothesis, writes and runs analysis, runs a backtest on point-in-time data, diagnoses the result, and decides what to test next.

 - Design rewards and evaluations that distinguish durable improvement from the artifacts of look-ahead bias, data leakage, overfitting, favorable execution assumptions, or hidden concentration and tail risk.

 - Train long-horizon agents to use data, research, coding, simulation, and portfolio tools while preserving provenance, respecting risk constraints, and adapting when market conditions change.

What you will own

 - Environments grounded in point-in-time data, realistic market mechanics, transaction costs, latency, capacity, and operational constraints.

 - Agents that conduct quantitative research, use analytical and execution tools, inspect their evidence, and recover from failed hypotheses.

 - Verifiers and evaluations that test robust out-of-sample behavior across assets, horizons, regimes, and adverse conditions.

 - Production loops with monitoring, human authority, regression gates, and failure attribution across models, data, simulation, and infrastructure, producing methods that transfer to other noisy, high-stakes decision systems.


REQUIREMENTS

 - We are looking first for depth in RL, agents, or post-training systems and the ability to become fluent in quantitative research.

 - Prior work in systematic trading, market microstructure, time-series modeling, econometrics, or financial simulation is useful but not required.

 - Hands-on experience building and debugging model-training, post-training, agent, evaluation, or closely adjacent experimental loops.

 - Strong experimental judgment: meaningful baselines, careful trace inspection, clear failure attribution, and a willingness to change direction when the evidence changes.

 - Strong Python and the ability to build artifacts that other researchers and engineers can run, inspect, and extend.

 - Comfort owning ambiguous problems and keeping partners and teammates current as you resolve them.

Evidence of exceptional work

We value publications, open-source systems, benchmarks, and shipped products as evidence of exceptional work. Show us something difficult you built, what failed, and how the evidence changed your approach.


WORK ARRANGEMENT

BENEFITS AND PERKS

 - Full medical, dental and vision coverage for employees and dependents.

 - $200/month health and wellness benefit.

 - Visa Sponsorship & relocation support

 - Company-covered meals when working from our San Francisco office.

If you're excited about the opportunity to build the foundation for the future of decentralized AI and create a platform that empowers developers and researchers to push the boundaries of what's possible, we'd love to hear from you.

As what you build matures, you'll hand it to new hires and trusted suppliers (likely including an office manager you'll lead). Your long-term remit will widen to global ops working closely with the Founders, whilst still retaining oversight on the NYC operation.

The motion is: build it, scale it, then manage it. The scope of the role grows as fast as the company does.

title: Sr. Research Associate
description:
About Us

We are a private design studio that builds and supports a portfolio of companies and projects across software, hardware, hospitality, and more. Some of what we build stays in house; some spins out. We also run an early-stage investment fund and an accompanying cohort program for founders. This company is not Expa, but is an affiliate of Expa's.

The Role

We're looking for a Senior Research Associate who can find out anything about anything. Leadership will come to you with questions — size this market, map the players in this category, who's funding what, what the landscape looks like for XYZ — and you'll come back with an answer that's clear, well-sourced, and actually useful.

Some weeks that means building a competitive matrix across 40 companies. Some weeks it means a deep dive into a single obscure question nobody has written about yet. The projects change, the subject matter changes, and the volume varies week to week.

You'll be exposed to a lot of different projects and ideas, and work directly with a highly accomplished leader and team. If you're the kind of person who reads everything, asks a lot of questions, and wants to be in the room with people operating at a very high level, this is built for you.

What You'll Do

 - Run open-ended research projects using the internet as your primary tool: markets, products, companies, funding activity, competitive landscapes, people, technologies, regulation — whatever the question requires.

 - Turn messy findings into clean outputs: matrices, comparison tables, briefs, landscape maps, one-pagers.

 - Go deep enough to have a point of view, not just a link dump — flag what matters, what's uncertain, and what you'd look at next.

 - Use AI tools aggressively to move faster and go wider than a person could alone.

 - Build lightweight tools, scrapers, or trackers when a project calls for it.

 - Juggle several unrelated requests at once and reprioritize when things shift.

What We're Looking For

 - 2–5 years of experience and a bachelor's degree — you take a task and run with it, but you've got the reps to produce senior-level output: quick turnaround, sharp judgment calls, and less hand-holding needed along the way.

 - Brain power: sharp, curious, and able to reason through a question you've never seen before.

 - AI-native: You live in AI tools — Claude and Cowork, ChatGPT, Gemini, Hugging Face, whatever's newest. Ideally you can vibe code your way to a working script or prototype without waiting on an engineer. Bonus points if you've hit your usage limit more than once.

 - Comfortable in ambiguity: Vague briefs don't paralyze you. You take a first pass, come back with questions, and iterate.

 - Self-directed but coachable: You think independently, but you want to learn from people far ahead of you and take direction well.

 - Startup-minded: You're not looking for a corporate ladder. You want interesting problems, smart people, and range.

 - A strong writer: Your research is only as good as your ability to communicate it in a page or less.

Compensation & Benefits

 - Salary: The anticipated base salary range for this position is $100,000-$130,000. Actual compensation will be determined based on factors including experience, qualifications, level, and location.

 - Benefits: Generous benefits package including medical, dental, and vision, 401(k) matching

 - Location: Can be remote in the US, with significant travel to Los Angeles

title: Financial Scriptwriter
description:
About Future Finance
 A capital-intelligence media brand - newsletter, LinkedIn, X and YouTube. Future Finance doesn't sell directly; it builds reach and credibility, then hands qualified demand to the rest of the group.
 The audience is US-based, 45-plus, net worth above $1M. They understand macro but don't know how to act on it - intelligent, busy, and sold to constantly.
 The brand register is calm, premium and institutional. It never slides into wealth-guru, outrage or doom media, because the audience we want won't trust that tone. This matters more than anything else in this hire.
 The role
 You write Future Finance's long-form YouTube scripts - 30 to 35 minutes, roughly 4,200 words, one per week - and own the research behind every claim in them, so every claim traces to a primary document. You also cut 3–4 short-form scripts from each episode for distribution.
 You do not pick topics and you do not own packaging (titles, thumbnails). That stays with the showrunner and the production agency. You do not name the channel's proprietary frameworks - those come from Salim. You may write about a mechanism he's already explained; you won't invent one and hand it to him to defend on camera.
 What success looks like
- One publish-ready script a week, minimum - four a month, delivered as a full package: research memo, six-beat hook, body, retention map, SHOW/SOURCE tags inline, self-scored review sheet.
- Clears the review gate at 7 of 9 or better on first submission, scored against the Future Finance Content Standard.
- Zero unsourced factual claims - every claim carries a SOURCE tag to a primary document, both sides of contested arguments get argued, and thin research gets flagged, never filled in with a plausible number.
- Retention targets on the finished episode - 70%+ first-minute retention, average view duration above the channel baseline.
- Compliance held on every script - no predictions, no recommendations, no certainty language about what happens next.
- Weekly execution - memo submitted ahead of packaging, attendance at the weekly review, Slack availability during working hours, deadline risk flagged the day it's known.
 Requirements 
 What we're looking for
- Sourcing discipline. You open the primary document, not the article about it, and can defend any claim in your own work on the spot.
- Finance literacy. You can read a 10-K, a central bank statement or a BIS paper and come out with an argument.
- Register control. You can raise a script's emotional voltage without reaching for wealth-guru or doom tools, and rewrite a hyped paragraph down without losing the stakes.
- Retention craft. You design open loops, pattern interrupts and a climax on purpose - and can draw the retention map because you built it that way.
- Writing for the ear. Scripted for a teleprompter: one idea per sentence, every term defined at first use, read aloud before submission.
- Comfort working inside someone else's frame. You flag a hole in the argument and stop - you don't hedge around it or quietly strengthen a claim the host can't defend.
- Proactivity, attention to detail, high standards, curiosity about macro and digital assets, and integrity about what you have and haven't checked.
 What you'll need to show us
 To reach an interview, you need to evidence all four of the following. We screen on evidence, not on our own read of the writing.
- Proven scale, in this category. Seven figures of cumulative views on finance, macro, investing or business long-form - or a verified 3x-plus outlier against a serious finance channel's trailing average. Must be 25-minute-plus long-form; short-form and 8-minute credits don't count. Retention data required (average view duration, first-minute retention - not view counts), shown live via YouTube Studio screenshare or confirmed by the channel owner. Screenshots alone, or channels you can't name, don't count.
- A high-value audience, not just a large one. What the channel sells, at what price, to whom - sponsor class and CPM are good proxies. Our viewer is 45-plus with $1M+ net worth.
- At least one sample in a calm, sourced, institutional register. If the whole portfolio is hype, get-rich or doom content, that's a disqualifier regardless of the numbers.
- Willingness to complete a paid work sample. One assigned title, five working days, $1,250 - paid whether or not we hire.
 How we'll hire
- Stage 1 - Past work review and interview. We read the actual work - not a summary or a list of links - against the four requirements above. If all four are evidenced, you move forward regardless of our personal taste in the writing.
- Stage 2 - Paid trial script. One assigned title, the Content Standard, five working days. Paid $1,250, whether or not you're hired - that's told upfront. You deliver: a research memo (two pages max, every claim sourced to a primary document, both sides of any contested argument argued); the hook (six beats, 70 words or fewer); the full script with SHOW cues and SOURCE tags inline; a retention map.
- Stage 3 - Contract → conversion. Trial script, then a contract which includes a 3 month trial period at the monthly rate, converting to a permanent seat on day 90 against the outcomes above.
 Benefits 
 What We Offer
- Competitive salary + performance-based incentives
- Company offsites
- Remote work
- High ownership, high-impact role

title: Research Associate - Data Curation
description:
Are you fascinated by the way science impacts society and do you love diving deep into the scientific literature? Do you enjoy curating data and extracting insights to help advance science? If you are a curious and rigorous data enthusiast, and want to help drug discovery scientists be more effective in creating new medicines, we want to hear from you! 
 Drug Hunter™ ( drughunter.com ) is an essential scientific intelligence platform for R&D innovators turning molecules into medicines. The Drug Hunter team distills the research behind emerging drugs and technologies into concise, but scientifically rich, searchable articles and interactive features. Drug Hunter customers include many of the world’s leading innovative biotechnology and pharmaceutical companies, as well as top-tier investors.
 We are seeking a rigorous data curator to join the Drug Hunter team to cover emerging drug discovery patents and other disclosures. For example, you will be responsible for triaging and curating data from scientific papers and patents, including interpreting chemical structures and biological data to surface the most important insights for our readers. The successful candidate will exhibit a high level of drug discovery scientific knowledge, with strong attention to detail and a keen focus on accuracy . An ability to interpret chemical structures and biological data is a must, as is experience reading the primary scientific and patent literature. 
 This role reports to a Scientific Director and is a full time , fully remote position for candidates based in North America.
 Key Responsibilities 
- Conduct in-depth research, curation, and interpretation of scientific data from the drug discovery-related scientific and patent literature
- Maintain high levels of rigor and accuracy in data curation and analysis, as well as the construction of databases
- Interpretation of chemical structures and biological data 
- Contribute to data research and curation across a range of projects 
- Maintain familiarity with the biopharmaceutical industry, including an understanding of the R&D process from target discovery to commercialization, and key players in the drug discovery and development ecosystem 
- Contribute to a positive culture within the Scientific and Data teams aligned with the mission and values of the company; prioritizing facts, community, clarity, helpfulness, teamwork, and accountability
 Additional Duties 
- Perform other related tasks as necessary to support the ongoing needs of Drug Hunter’s Scientific and Data teams, and associated functions
 Requirements 
 Qualifications 
- Authorization to work in the employee’s location. Drug Hunter cannot provide US visa/Green Card sponsorship or related support relevant to the employee’s location.
- Strong track record of data curation, with an understanding of the patent processes and patent databases
- Ability to interpret chemical structures and biological data, as well as a familiarity with ChemDraw or similar chemical drawing software
- Experience using spreadsheets, such as Excel, Google Sheets, or LibreOffice Calc
- Familiarity with scientific databases and chemoinformatics resources, such as PubChem, PubMed, ClinicalTrials.gov , ChEMBL, SureChEMBL, etc.
- Basic understanding of regulatory agencies and their databases (e.g., the FDA)
- Excellent written and verbal communication abilities with both technical and non-technical audiences, including fluency in English
- Comfort working in a fast-paced, collaborative, start-up environment, working with colleagues and collaborators across disciplines, and tackling novel challenges
- Digitally native, comfortable with social media, software, and new technologies and platforms, and eager to apply new best practices to a growing organization
- Demonstrated ability to pick up new fields of expertise quickly and work with agility in a growth environment
- Candidates with a basic understanding of Python for data processing and automation will be preferred
 Education and Experience 
- A B.S. or M.S. (or equivalent) in organic chemistry, medicinal chemistry, or chemical biology
- 0-3 years of experience focused on data curation; preference is given to candidates with experience from biotechnology or pharmaceutical companies

Jupiter is the global market leader in analytics for resilience planning and enterprise climate risk management.  We are led by pioneers in data, climate, and earth and ocean sciences, as well as technology, risk management, company building, and public policy. Jupiter is bringing diversity to prepare a diverse planet for our changing climate. Jupiter was founded on the principle that with the right approaches and the right team, we can prepare Earth’s economies to meet the challenges associated with climate change. The world is a diverse place; a diverse workforce in an inclusive environment is essential to meet our goals. We go forward together.

Join Jupiter's Product organization to help build the risk engine behind our economic modeling. Working directly with the Principal PM, for Economic & Financial Modeling, you will translate climate hazard data into actionable financial metrics like EBITDA impact, CapEx/OpEx, and credit risk. 
This is an associate-level, development-focused contract role designed for someone with solid Python and data engineering skills alongside a foundation in economics or finance. You will spend your time building and scaling model infrastructure while expanding your financial domain knowledge on the job through direct mentorship. 


What You Will Do
- Build & Scale Pipelines: Write modular, well-tested Python code to move models from research prototypes into production pipelines across large company and asset datasets. 
- Support Model Research: Assist in prototyping statistical, econometric, and machine learning models (e.g., time-series analysis, regression) to project climate hazard impacts. 
- Data Engineering: Source, clean, and transform diverse financial, building, and hazard datasets, resolving missing data or anomalies. 
- Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with engineering, product, and client teams to document outputs and communicate analytical findings clearly.

What You Will Bring

About Anthropic 
 Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
 Anthropic Fellows Program overview 
 The Anthropic Fellows Program is designed to foster AI research and engineering talent. We provide funding and mentorship to promising technical talent - regardless of previous experience.
 Fellows will primarily use external infrastructure (e.g. open-source models, public APIs) to work on project aligned with our research priorities, with the goal of producing a public output (e.g. a paper submission). In one of our earlier cohorts, over 80% of fellows produced papers. We run multiple cohorts of Fellows each year and review applications on a rolling basis.
 Submit your application to the Economics & Policy workstream at the bottom of this page. We are accepting applications on a rolling basis for the next cohort expected to start in January 2027. In some circumstances, we can accommodate fellows starting outside the usual cohort timelines — please note in your application if the January 2027 start date doesn't work for you.
 What to expect 
- 4 months of full-time research 
- Direct mentorship from Anthropic researchers 
- Weekly stipend of 4,615 USD / 3,440 GBP / 6,470 CAD / 4,110 EUR + benefits (these vary by country)
- Substantial funding for compute and other research expenses
 Interview process 
 The interview process will include an initial application, assessments, and interviews. We may ask for references later in the process as well.
 We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.
 Compensation 
 The expected base stipend for this role is 4,615 USD / 3,440 GBP / 6,470 CAD / 4,110 EUR per week, with an expectation of 40 hours per week for 4 months (with possible extension).
 The Anthropic Institute Fellows (Economics & Policy) 
 Mentors, research areas, & past projects 
 Fellows will undergo a project selection & mentor matching process. Potential research areas and mentors include:
- Economics 
- Maxim Massenkoff
- Peter McCrory
- Policy, Security, and Society 
- Jack Clark
- Marina Favaro
- Jim Baker
 Projects in this workstream may include:
- Designing and conducting empirical research on AI's economic effects, drawing on external data sources
- Developing new methodological approaches for studying AI's impact on labor markets, the future of work, and society
- Analysing the offense–defense balance for AI-enabled cyber and bio capabilities as models scale
- Measuring the extent to which model performance increases with custom harnesses
- Identifying market driven mechanisms that could improve societal resilience to anticipated threats from AI systems
- Identifying which metrics relating to AI R&D could serve as early warning signals for recursive self-improvement
 For past project examples, see:
- How AI Impacts Skill Formation : Judy Shen and Alex Tamkin
- Stress-Testing Model Specs Reveals Character Differences among Language Models : Jifan Zhang, Henry Sleight, Andi Peng, John Schulman, and Esin Durmus

- Place equipment finance transactions with existing funding partners

- Help identify the best funding sources based on transaction quality and market appetite
- Support the expansion of the company’s capital partner network as volume grows
- Track funding trends and market demand within equipment finance
- Assist in building a broader capital markets and syndication function over time

Qualifications 
- 2+ years of experience in capital markets, syndication, banking, equipment finance, structured finance, or a related field
- Buy-side or sell-side capital markets experience is acceptable
- Understanding of debt placement and institutional funding relationships
- Strong communication and relationship management skills
- Comfortable working in a growing, entrepreneurial environment
- Equipment finance experience is a plus
 Ideal Background 
- Background with a bank, financial institution, or similar platform
- Early-career to mid-level professional looking for growth potential
- Interested in joining a company where they can stand out and help build the function
- Motivated by the opportunity to grow into a Capital Markets Manager or Director-level role over time
 Compensation 
- Base salary plus incentive opportunity
- Growth-oriented role with increasing upside as the business scales
- This is a strong opportunity to join a growing equipment finance platform with attractive credits, strong marketability, and meaningful long-term upside.

 Founded in 2004 by investment bankers, Wall Street Prep (WSP) is a leading provider of professional skills training in financial and valuation modeling.  Wall Street Prep is seeking an experienced and enthusiastic AI for Finance Instructor with a strong background in applying artificial intelligence, machine learning, and automation in business and finance settings. As an AI Instructor, you will join our elite team of instructors delivering cutting-edge training to professionals and students eager to master AI tools for real-world decision-making and business transformation.

title: Senior Finance Consultant: Corporate Strategy & Research - Remote Advisory (Kraków)
description:
Senior Finance Consultant: Corporate Strategy & Research (Remote Advisory)
 About Prolific 
 Prolific is not just another player in the AI space – we are building the biggest pool of quality human data in the world.
 Over 35,000 AI developers, researchers, and organizations use Prolific to gather data from paid study participants with a wide variety of experiences, knowledge, and skills.
 The role 
 We are seeking Director, VP, and C-Level Finance Professionals to join our expert B2B and AI research network. We provide high-level corporate intelligence for global organizations, and we require executive-level insights to validate complex financial data.
Please note: This is an invitation to join our expert talent pool. Participation in specific projects is not guaranteed and is subject to client demand and profile matching.
 Please note, you will be asked to provide your LinkedIn profile URL when joining the waitlist so we can verify your experience.
 Researchers looking for your skills tend to pay up to $100 You must be prepared to complete paid tasks that require one hour of uninterrupted work , though many are shorter.
 What you’ll bring 
- 
 Executive tenure: Proven track record at the Director level or above (CFO, VP, etc.).
- 
 Specialized knowledge: Deep expertise in corporate fiscal strategy, auditing, or financial modeling.
- 
 Professional profile: A verifiable LinkedIn presence or professional history. attention to detail and the ability to concentrate on complex tasks for up to one hour at a time
- 
 A reliable and fast internet connection and access to a computer
- 
 A willingness to self-declare your earnings, as our participants are self-employed
- 
 A Paypal account to receive payment from our clients
 What you’ll be doing in the role 
- 
 Strategic document audit: Review comprehensive financial reports (200–300 pages) to identify key fiscal drivers.
- 
 Executive consulting: Answer nuanced questions regarding corporate finance, risk, and strategy based on provided data.
- 
 B2B validation: Ensure research outputs reflect the practical realities of high-level financial management. willingness to take our skills verification test to assess your suitability for our participant pool
 Why Prolific is a great platform to join as a Participant 
 Joining our platform as a Prolific participant will give you the chance to influence the AI models of the future using professional legal expertise. Once you pass our assessment, you can join Prolific in just 15 minutes, and start enjoying competitive pay rates, flexible hours, and the ability to work from home.
 We've built a unique platform that connects researchers and companies with a global pool of participants, enabling the collection of high-quality, ethically sourced human behavioural data and feedback. This data is the cornerstone of developing more accurate, nuanced, and aligned AI systems.
 We believe that the next leap in AI capabilities won't come solely from scaling existing models, but from integrating diverse human perspectives and behaviours into AI development. By providing this crucial human data infrastructure, Prolific is positioning itself at the forefront of the next wave of AI innovation – one that reflects the breadth and the best of humanity.

 What Success Looks Like

title: Financial Crimes Analyst
description:
Few people get to build a bank from scratch. Even fewer get to build one at a moment when banking itself is being reinvented.


The Dollar is the best product in the history of the world - there is infinite global demand. But international fintechs and banks are left with two unsatisfying options to choose from: Either build on legacy correspondent banks that are slow and unreliable, or interface with middleware providers that neither move nor hold the dollars directly, but instead rely on underlying legacy banks themselves. At Augustus, we collapse the stack by combining two things: A real, national bank charter (in organization), and Marble, our proprietary core banking system, built around intelligence, made of code.


We are a group of ex-founders, founding employees of unicorns, and people who dropped out of university because they believe this is an industry and career defining opportunity. We are backed with more than $200M from Peter Thiel's Valar Ventures, Tiger Global, Hummingbird, QED, Creandum, and the founders of Nubank, Ramp, Deel, Circle, Fluidstack, Fuse, and Etched.


We are regulated in Europe and live with Euro and Stablecoin clearing today. Now, we are building the US team from the ground up, while continuing to grow rapidly in Europe.




THE ROLE

As a Financial Crimes Analyst at Augustus, you own transaction monitoring end to end, from alert to final disposition. You clear alerts, run case investigations and draft SARs. You find new typologies and turn them into rules.

We’re building an AI native bank, which is designed to run mostly autonomously. Legacy banks scale transaction monitoring with people. We scale it with agents, supporting human decisions. You improve the prompts of our alert review agents, tune monitoring rules to cut false positives, and work with Engineering and Product to automate investigations within our regulatory bounds. Your judgment sets the standard the agents follow. The goal is to make routine alerts disappear so your time goes to the cases that matter.

 


YOUR FIRST SIX MONTHS

 - Months 1-2: Work the queue yourself. Clear transaction monitoring alerts end to end: review, disposition and escalation. Learn the Bank’s TM program and rule logic well enough to see where rules misfire and where the review agents get it wrong.

Sierra is the leading platform for customer-facing AI agents, working with many of the world's biggest brands — including The GAP, Rocket Mortgage, SoFi, Sutter Health, and SoftBank — to transform how they serve customers and grow their businesses. The decisions we make impact millions of end customers and billions of dollars in economic activity.

 - Our financial services team partners closely with these organizations to set their AI strategies and build modern tools that carefully handle moments when a person’s private anxiety meets an institution’s procedural muscle - the instant before a family learns whether they are pre-approved for a mortgage; the claustrophobic half hour after someone notices a fraudulent charge; the frustrating experience of losing a card and needing to order a new one.

 - Sierra’s Financial Services team is transforming the customer experience and building technology that makes the industry more accessible, human, and affordable for everyone.


WHAT YOU’LL DO

As an Agent Strategist https://sierra.ai/blog/agent-strategist-your-phd-in-applied-ai, you own how Sierra’s AI agents come to life for our customers — from first pilot to a production agent handling thousands of conversations a day. You sit at the intersection of product, building agents and customer-facing work, and stay just as close to the technology as you are to the people you build for. Take agents from initial scope through conversation design, tooling, and evaluation, to launch and continuous iteration in production — translating business goals into an agent that outperforms, and tuning relentlessly until it’s the best version of itself in the real world. You’ll have real ownership and autonomy over the outcome.

 - Be the trusted strategic advisor to enterprise leaders. Sit shoulder-to-shoulder with our customers’ executives, understand what success actually means to their business, and shape the AI strategy that gets them there.

 - Partner with the customer’s working teams day to day. Run working sessions, troubleshoot the agent as issues come up, and make the calls that keep the build on track for launch.

 - Directly impact product. Surface unmet needs from your customer work, and feed them back to research and platform to shape where Sierra goes next.


EXAMPLE PROJECTS

These are the kinds of projects that strategists on our team have worked on recently:

 - Scope and launch a subscription-retention agent for a large telecommunications or media company that consistently outperforms human agents at saving at-risk customers.

 - Stand up an agent for a commerce customer that troubleshoots a broken device end-to-end and personalizes product recommendations in the same conversation.

 - You’ve been a founder, founding team member, or operator — you know how to balance craft, ownership, and speed.
